title: Estimation of Online Fan Perception Scores for Korean Professional Baseball Managers Using Machine Learning-Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: 이 연구의 목적은 소셜 빅데이터와 머신러닝 기반 감성분석을 활용하여 한국프로야구 감독에 대한 온라인 팬 인식을 분석하고, 감독별 긍정·부정 인식점수를 산출하는 것이다. 이 연구의 목적을 달성하기 위해서 동영상 플랫폼 유튜브에서 2025년 3월 22일을 기준으로 한 달간 한국프로야구 하이라이트 영상에 달린 총 53,718건의 댓글을 수집하였다. 자료수집은 유튜브 API를 활용하여 Python 3 기반 웹 크롤링 자동화 프로그램을 사용하였다. 수집된 자료 중 감독과 관련된 2,154건의 댓글을 최종 분석 대상으로 선별하였으며, 댓글 자료를 토큰화한 후 명사, 동사, 형용사만 추출하였다. 추출한 단어 중 공통어, 불용어를 전처리한 후 BOW(Bag of Words) 방법을 활용하여 텍스트 데이터를 정형화하였다. 이후 LASSO(Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator)를 적용하여 주요 감성어를 선별하고, 로지스틱 회귀모형으로 댓글별 긍정·부정 감성확률을 예측하여 감독별 온라인 팬 인식점수를 산출하였다. 분석 결과, 한국프로야구 감독의 긍정점수는 26.2점으로 나타났으며, 부정점수는 73.8점으로 나타났다. 10개 구단 중 LG 트윈스 감독이 긍정점수 55.0점, 부정점수 45.0점으로 가장 높은 점수를 받았으며, KIA 타이거즈 감독이 긍정점수 14.6점, 부정점수 85.4점으로 가장 낮은 점수를 받았다. 결론적으로 이 연구는 소셜미디어 댓글 분석을 통해 한국프로야구 감독에 대한 온라인 팬 인식의 형성 양상을 보여주었으며, 감독 관련 팬 인식을 정량적으로 파악할 수 있는 기초자료로 활용될 것이다.

title: AI for prognostic assessment of diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma using H&E whole‐slide images
abstract: Abstract Prediction of the outcome of large B‐cell lymphomas/high‐grade B‐cell lymphomas (DLBCLs/HGBCLs) is based on clinical parameters and molecular testing, for example, for rearrangements of MYC (MYC‐R) and MYC‐R in combination with BCL2 and BCL6 translocations (double/triple hit). However, the group of DLBCL/HGBCL with poor outcome is not confined to MYC‐R lymphomas, and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) testing for MYC‐R misses several high‐risk lymphomas. We aimed to understand if artificial intelligence (AI) trained to identify MYC‐R will delineate a poor prognostic subgroup. We generated a collection of digital hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)‐stained slides of DLBCL/HGBCL ( N = 2018) annotated for MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 translocations. A multiple‐instance deep learning AI model for the identification of MYC‐R alone or as double/triple hit was established using 1035 H&E‐stained slides and evaluated on an external test cohort ( N = 499). A pretrained tumor tissue classifier improved reliability and interpretability by focusing the model on tumor areas. Our model score reflects a morphological “MYCness” in DLBCL/HGBCL and demonstrates a strong association with overall survival (OS) and progression‐free survival (PFS) in the external test cohort. This was confirmed with an additional clinical test cohort ( N = 484) without FISH labels. The AI model scores correlate with various molecular features of DLBCL/HGBCL, including BCL2 and MYC gene expression, and the high‐grade gene expression signature, but also features of the tumor microenvironment. Multivariate analysis, adjusted for International Prognostic Index (IPI) factors, demonstrated the prognostic significance of our model in identifying high‐risk cases for both PFS and OS.

This was confirmed with an additional clinical test cohort ( N = 484) without FISH labels. The AI model scores correlate with various molecular features of DLBCL/HGBCL, including BCL2 and MYC gene expression, and the high‐grade gene expression signature, but also features of the tumor microenvironment. Multivariate analysis, adjusted for International Prognostic Index (IPI) factors, demonstrated the prognostic significance of our model in identifying high‐risk cases for both PFS and OS.

title: Generalized Bayesian Clustering with Regression for Unaligned Longitudinal Binary Data
abstract: We propose a generalized Bayesian clustering with regression model for unaligned longitudinal binary outcomes, motivated by seizure diary data from the Human Epilepsy Project. Seizure diaries are sparse, irregularly observed, and vary enormously across patients. A single fully-specified generative model tends to be either misspecified or computationally inefficient. We address the challenge by two strategies. We set up a regression by way of clustering as model-based clustering using a mixture model. For the latter, we take a generalized Bayesian perspective which replaces the full likelihood with a loss-based update using a generalized likelihood. We combine a trajectory similarity loss and a regression loss, so that clustering is informed by both trajectory similarity and the prediction of outcomes The trajectory similarity loss is constructed by representing each trajectory as an (empirical) distribution of subsequences, called reads, and then is defined based on the sliced Wasserstein distance between these empirical distributions. This loss allows alignment-free comparison of sequences that are irregularly observed or temporally misaligned, and it scales quasi-linearly in trajectory length. The regression loss is the negative log-likelihood of a probit regression. A prior on the cluster-specific parameters is defined by way of a Dirichlet process prior on the mixing measure.

title: Likelihood-Constrained Acoustic Reranking for Training-Free Hallucination Mitigation in LLM-Based ASR
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems achieve strong performance on conventional speech data by leveraging powerful linguistic priors and multilingual capabilities. However, under challenging conditions, these priors can override acoustic evidence, resulting in unintended translation, instruction execution, repetition, or catastrophic deletion. We propose Likelihood-Constrained Acoustic Reranking (LCAR), a training-free decoding method that improves acoustic grounding while preserving support from the base model. At each decoding step, LCAR first retains tokens whose base-model likelihood falls within a margin of the greedy token, then reranks them using an acoustic compatibility score computed from attention-pooled audio embeddings and the existing LM head. By restricting acoustic intervention to plausible, model-supported alternatives, LCAR requires no additional training, external detector, reference transcript, or auxiliary model at inference. We evaluate LCAR on four LLM-based ASR systems using human-audited TTS and open-source speech challenge suites. At $δ=0.60$, LCAR removes 38.8--57.1\% of detector-identified hallucination failures while largely maintaining WER/CER on standard open-source test sets.

title: Will the User Ever Know? Covert Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Tool-Using LLM Agents
abstract: As LLM agents take real-world actions through tools, indirect prompt injection (IPI) has emerged as a serious threat. The standard metric, Attack Success Rate (ASR), counts whether an injection succeeds but ignores what the user notices in the agent's final response. Looking at successful injection traces, we find two distinct outcomes: the agent executes the injection while returning an otherwise normal response, or reports the injected action in its final response, giving the user a chance to notice. We call these covert and overt successes. From the user's perspective, we decompose ASR into the Covert Success Rate (CSR), counting successes leaving no trace in the final response, and the Overt Success Rate (OSR), counting successes the user can detect. To understand what drives the gap, we analyze successful trajectories and find that the agent's behavior after the injection separates covert from overt: covert traces hand control back to the user task before ending, while overt traces end at the attack itself. This split follows from the ReAct format, where the final response summarizes the most recent action. Building on this observation, we propose ICoA (Induced Covert Attack), an IPI attack designed to induce covert outcomes by steering the agent back to the user task after executing the injection. Across four target models on AgentDojo, ICoA achieves the highest CSR, with gains of 3.79-12.01 percentage points over the strongest baseline.

title: Enhancing AI Dialogue through Dual Role Assignment: An Investigation of User-AI Professional Role Sharing
abstract: Conversational AI systems increasingly employ role/persona prompting to elicit domain-specific responses, yet roles are typically assigned only to the AI side while the user remains a neutral questioner. This study empirically investigates how dialogue content transforms when professional roles are assigned not only to the AI but also to the user, and when both parties share the same role. We conducted controlled dialogues about an identical line-drawing stimulus under four role-assignment conditions (no-role, AI-only role, user-only role, and both roles) across five professional roles (detective, psychologist, artist, architect, natural scientist) and four contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, OpenAI o1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro), yielding 64 sessions and 320 question–response pairs. Quantitative term-frequency analysis of the detective role—presented as a representative case with the clearest lexical shifts—revealed that the shared-role condition increased domain-specific terminology compared to baseline and single-role conditions, a pattern also observed in the other four roles. Qualitative close readings of the detective role suggested that shared roles were associated with stronger expertise-oriented reasoning, multiperspectivity, and characteristics resembling professional peer exchange. Notably, user-side role assignment alone altered model responses even without an explicit AI role instruction. Cross-model comparisons under the shared detective-role condition showed that each LLM expressed the same role frame with distinct stylistic tendencies, supporting a two-layer interaction model in which externally imposed role frames set the discourse direction while model-specific traits shape expression style. These findings offer practical implications for prompt engineering, educational dialogue design, and expert-support systems. The full dataset is publicly available on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.14567800).

title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Improving the Efficiency of Administrative Decision-Making within Iraqi Provincial Sports Clubs
abstract: ABSTRACT The research aims to identify the role of artificial intelligence in improving the quality of administrative decisions. In order to achieve this goal, the dimensions of artificial intelligence (appropriate training and development, effectiveness) were adopted, as well as the dimensions of the administrative decision: the time dimension, the quality of the decision, and the acceptance of the decision. The importance of the research stems from the importance of the administrative decision for organizations and the major role it plays in providing solutions to problems and choosing alternatives that serve the organization's goals. Artificial intelligence is also one of the most important factors that lead to the creation of knowledge and ideas that contribute to improving the decision-making process. The study population consists of a sample of managers in Asia Cell Telecommunications Company, consisting of fifty managers. By adopting the descriptive analytical method, the statistical results of the research confirmed the validity of the research hypothesis, which is that there is an impact of artificial intelligence on improving the quality of administrative decisions in Iraqi provincial sports clubs, as the clubs rely on the application of an artificial intelligence-based program, through the application of artificial intelligence programs by administrative leaders using a computer network that connects the main center with the branches. Accordingly, it was recommended to focus more on attracting and selecting candidates for employment who have scientific and practical experience in the field of artificial intelligence, as well as training employees on the efficiency of using artificial intelligence programs and their applications.

title: Structure without semantics: derived cohort, analysis code and results ledger
abstract: Code, derived cohort and complete results ledger for a study testing whether the semantic content of feature groups drives performance in group-aware tabular transformers. Across 24 randomly permuted partitions on two independent cross-validation folds, semantically meaningful feature groups perform no better than meaningless ones of the same sizes, and no group count from one to sixteen separates from another. A companion analysis quantifies how supplying a model with the variables that define its own outcome inflates apparent accuracy from 0.832 to 0.996 and inverts the ranking of models, so the weakest appears strongest. Source data are public files from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (cycles 2011-2012 through 2017-2018) and require no application or credentialling. The derived analysis cohort (19,978 adults, 40 columns) rebuilds byte-identically from them using the deposited construction script. The results ledger deliberately retains superseded values alongside their replacements. Four findings in this study reversed under scrutiny, and the reversals can be audited from the files here rather than taken on the manuscript's word. An independent re-execution record is included: the cohort rebuilds to an identical checksum from re-downloaded source files, and the permutation test and factorial reproduce bit-identically across 16 and 20 runs respectively. Contents: cohort construction, the model implementation with its ordinal Dirichlet evidential objective, every experimental runner with its stored results, figure scripts and outputs, a complete manifest, per-file checksums, and a pinned environment specification.

title: Linear Matrix Systems and Quantum Algorithms
abstract: Linear matrix systems represent a fundamental class of problems in mathematics, physics, and engineering, and their efficient solution is crucial for various applications. Traditional methods often rely on computationally intensive algorithms, limiting scalability. This paper explores the potential of leveraging the inherent non-linear properties of linear matrices to design novel quantum algorithms for solving linear systems. We propose a quantum algorithm predicated on the principle that by mapping a linear system into a non-linear representation via a specific matrix transformation, we can achieve speedups that surpass classical approaches. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum circuit that systematically explores this non-linear space, leveraging quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to enhance the search process. The paper details the design of a quantum algorithm for solving linear systems, emphasizing the benefits of this approach and its potential to unlock new possibilities in quantum computation.

title: 基于循环神经网络的自适应自映射算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive self-mapping (SAM) algorithm leveraging the power of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to achieve data mapping and feature extraction. The algorithm dynamically adjusts data features based on the inherent cyclical structure within the input data, enhancing model performance and efficiency. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through successful application in image processing and data compression tasks, highlighting its potential for improved representation and generalization. The core mechanism involves a recurrent layer within the neural network, which learns the cyclical patterns and maps them to the input data. This adaptation process results in more effective feature extraction and representation, surpassing traditional methods. This work contributes to the advancement of efficient feature learning techniques and opens avenues for novel applications across diverse domains.

title: Recursive Quantum Degradation Coding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel recursive quantum degradation coding (RQDC) framework designed to achieve efficient quantum information compression and transmission under limited quantum resources. The core concept involves constructing a recursive encoding structure leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition. This structure operates across multiple hierarchical levels, performing iterative compression and transmission with integrated feedback mechanisms for error correction. Unlike existing approaches that rely on predefined encoding schemes, the RQDC framework exhibits inherent adaptability and robustness. The method aims to mitigate the detrimental effects of channel degradation by dynamically adjusting the encoding parameters at each level. Mathematical models are presented to illustrate the key principles and performance characteristics of the RQDC framework. The framework's ability to adaptively manage information loss through recursive processing offers a promising avenue for practical quantum communication and storage. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated through theoretical analysis and simulation, demonstrating its potential to achieve significant compression ratios while maintaining acceptable fidelity.

title: Dynamic Geometric Mapping for Quantum Feature Extraction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum feature extraction based on dynamic geometric mapping. Traditional feature extraction methods often rely on classical computational techniques, limiting their ability to fully exploit the inherent quantum properties of data. We propose a new method that leverages quantum entanglement to represent and extract features, offering a fundamentally different perspective. This approach utilizes a dynamic geometric mapping to translate data into a quantum state, enabling a more nuanced and efficient extraction process. The core mechanism centers around simulating quantum feature extraction through the interplay of entangled geometric relationships. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results, showcasing a significant improvement in feature extraction accuracy and speed compared to conventional approaches. The fundamental insight lies in harnessing quantum entanglement to guide the data transformation, providing a powerful tool for quantum data analysis.

title: Title: Non-Linear Feedback via Fractal Iteration in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper explores the application of fractal iteration within neural networks to enhance generalization and robustness against overfitting. Traditional neural network training often suffers from sensitivity to initial conditions and the tendency to overfit, particularly in complex datasets. We propose a novel feedback loop mechanism, termed "Fractal Iteration Rate," that dynamically adjusts this rate to promote more stable and robust learning. The core idea is to utilize fractal iteration to iteratively refine the network's internal representation, effectively creating a self-correcting mechanism that minimizes sensitivity to noisy data and encourages a more generalizable model. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and a preliminary analysis of a simplified neural network architecture. The focus is on fostering a learning process that is less prone to catastrophic forgetting and exhibits improved performance across a range of challenging datasets.

title: Adaptive Kernel Methods for Non-Stationary Data Streams
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive kernel method designed specifically for handling non-stationary data streams. Traditional kernel methods often struggle when the underlying data distribution changes over time, leading to diminished performance and inaccurate predictions. Our approach addresses this limitation by continuously learning and updating the kernel parameters based on the incoming data. This dynamic adjustment allows the method to adapt to evolving environments, maintaining accuracy even as the data stream shifts. The core claim centers on the sensitivity of traditional kernel methods to distribution changes. The proposed mechanism leverages a streaming learning framework to build a kernel function that optimizes for the current data state. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this adaptive approach, focusing on the convergence properties of the learning algorithm and the impact of the kernel parameter updates on prediction accuracy. We present a mathematical formulation of the adaptive kernel method, outlining the key equations and notations. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through a conceptual analysis and theoretical justification, highlighting its potential for real-world applications where data streams are inherently non-stationary.

abstract: Quantum Graph Theory (QGT) offers a promising paradigm shift in cybersecurity, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to enhance data protection and security. This paper investigates the application of QGT to network security, focusing on the detection of malicious nodes, vulnerabilities, and key distribution attacks. We propose a novel framework incorporating graph algorithms and quantum cryptography to create a robust defense against evolving cyber threats. The core mechanism involves analyzing network graphs, identifying anomalous patterns, and utilizing quantum-enhanced data verification to mitigate potential attacks. The paper details the fundamental concepts, the proposed framework, and the expected benefits of integrating QGT with existing cybersecurity protocols. We also discuss the challenges and future research directions for this field.

title: Deep Learning for Automated Theorem Proving – Symbolic Reasoning from Neural Representations
abstract: This paper explores the potential of deep learning techniques for automating theorem proving. The core idea is to leverage neural networks to learn a symbolic reasoning process, effectively mimicking the steps involved in constructing a formal proof. We propose a model where a neural network, denoted as *N*, is trained to predict the next logical step given the current state of a proof. The input to *N* is represented as (s1, s2, ..., sK), where *K* represents the current proof state. The output of *N* is a predicted step, *sK+1*, which is then added to the proof, and the process repeats. The model is trained using a loss function that measures the difference between the predicted step and the correct step in a known proof. This approach offers a novel way to bridge the gap between the strengths of traditional symbolic reasoning and the pattern recognition abilities of deep learning, potentially leading to more robust and efficient automated theorem provers. The key contributions of this work lie in the methodology for representing proof states in a neural network-compatible format and the training strategy for enabling the network to learn a coherent logical reasoning process.

title: Adaptive Chaos in Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Adaptive Chaos, a novel training algorithm, to enhance neural network training through dynamic adjustment of learning rate and regularization strength. We hypothesize that neural networks exhibit chaotic behavior, generating unpredictable fluctuations in their parameter space. Our approach, "Chaotic Gradient Descent," leverages this instability to optimize the network's learning process, leading to improved generalization and robustness. We present a theoretical framework demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness in mitigating overfitting and enhancing the network's ability to generalize to unseen data. This work explores a unique method of monitoring and responding to chaotic dynamics within the parameter space, offering a potential paradigm shift in neural network training.

title: Black-fronted Duiker Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BDI-MHA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Black-fronted Duiker Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BDI-MHA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-fronted duiker ( *Sylvicapra frontalis*). The algorithm leverages the duiker's adaptive movement strategy – a combination of exploratory and exploitative phases – to optimize complex problems. BDI-MHA incorporates a dynamic exploration rate, influenced by the duiker's response to environmental changes, and a memory-based exploitation phase mimicking the animal's preference for previously successful food sources. The algorithm's core features include a novel position update mechanism based on a weighted average of the best solution and a randomly generated solution, along with an adaptive inertia weight scheme. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's convergence properties and its potential for improved performance compared to traditional metaheuristic methods. The algorithm is tested on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function, showcasing its effectiveness and efficiency. The results indicate that BDI-MHA consistently outperforms other common metaheuristic algorithms in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. Future research will focus on parameter tuning and further exploration of the algorithm's adaptability to different problem domains.

title: Explainable AI for Reinforcement Learning through Counterfactual Analysis
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable success in solving complex tasks, from playing games to controlling robots. However, the "black box" nature of many RL algorithms – the lack of interpretability regarding *why* an agent makes a particular decision – presents a significant challenge. This paper proposes a novel approach to explain RL agent behavior through counterfactual analysis. We introduce a technique that generates "what-if" scenarios by systematically altering a single variable in the environment and observing the resulting impact on the agent's actions. By examining the causal relationships revealed through these counterfactuals, we can gain insight into the factors driving the agent's decision-making process. This approach offers a direct and interpretable method for debugging, improving, and ultimately understanding the underlying logic of RL agents. The core idea is to shift from simply observing outcomes to actively probing the causal links between variables and actions. This work lays the foundation for building more trustworthy and reliable RL systems.

title: ## Big-eared Free-tailed Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bat Echo Optimization Algorithm" (BEOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of big-eared free-tailed bats ( *Bigiella aurantica*). These bats utilize sophisticated echolocation techniques to navigate and locate food sources in complex environments. The BEOA leverages the core principles of bat echolocation – frequency modulation, phase angle adjustment, and echo intensity – to effectively explore and optimize solutions in a given search space. The algorithm employs a population of "bats" representing potential solutions, iteratively adjusting their positions based on echo characteristics (simulated by fitness evaluation) and a "home" position representing the best known solution. The algorithm's parameters, including the echo intensity, phase angle adjustment rate, and home position influence, are designed to mimic the adaptive behavior of the bats. The performance of the BEOA is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive performance against established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's ability to adapt to varying landscape topologies and its relatively simple implementation make it a potentially valuable tool for a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Computation Paradigm
abstract: Quantum Topology Adaptive Computation Paradigm addresses the challenges of complex quantum computation by proposing a novel computational framework that integrates quantum topology with adaptive computation. This framework leverages the inherent self-similarity and topological properties of quantum systems to enable highly efficient and adaptable quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around a dynamic, self-configuring computational paradigm that dynamically adjusts to the specific properties of the underlying quantum system, optimizing for computational complexity and enabling novel algorithmic designs. This research aims to establish a new paradigm for quantum computation, moving beyond traditional static approaches and offering enhanced capabilities for complex problems.

title: Spectral-Based Computation Security
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to computation security leveraging the principles of spectral theory. Traditional computational security relies heavily on cryptographic methods, which are increasingly vulnerable to advancements in computing power and algorithmic attacks. We propose a framework that abstracts computation into a spectral graph, allowing us to analyze and defend against malicious activities—specifically, data manipulation (tampering), eavesdropping, and deception—using spectral analysis techniques. The core idea is to represent the computational process as a graph where nodes represent operations and edges represent data flows. Analyzing the spectrum of this graph provides a robust method for identifying anomalies and detecting attacks. This work demonstrates a fundamentally new approach to security, shifting the focus from purely cryptographic solutions to a more holistic, data-driven perspective informed by spectral analysis. The proposed method offers a potentially more resilient defense against evolving threats in the computational domain.

title: Title: Topological Quantum Entanglement (TQE)
abstract: This paper investigates Topological Quantum Entanglement (TQE), a novel approach to quantum computation centered around the manipulation of topological quantum states. We propose a robust algorithm, the "Topology Map" method, designed to generate and manipulate complex, multi-layered quantum states with inherent resilience to noise. The core claim is that this methodology, leveraging the principles of topological quantum mechanics, will significantly enhance quantum computation by reducing error rates and enabling the creation of more stable and powerful quantum systems. We detail the algorithm's mechanics, the underlying topological properties leveraged, and the potential benefits of this approach compared to existing quantum technologies. The work explores the challenges and opportunities presented by utilizing topology to address inherent vulnerabilities in current quantum states.

title: Quantum Entanglement Based on Dynamic Topology Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon with profound implications for quantum information processing. This paper explores the design of a novel quantum computing model predicated on dynamic topology, aiming to surpass the limitations of classical quantum computation. The core mechanism involves establishing a dynamic topology model that encodes and manipulates quantum information through its inherent structure. We propose a framework that leverages the unique properties of entangled states to enable the implementation of advanced quantum algorithms, including enhanced quantum cryptography and improved quantum simulation capabilities. This research investigates the potential of this approach to unlock new levels of computational complexity and offers a promising path toward future quantum technologies.

title: The Transparent Jellyfish-Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (TJEAE)
abstract: This paper introduces the Transparent Jellyfish-Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (TJEAE), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique swimming behavior of transparent jellyfish. These organisms utilize a complex, undulating motion to efficiently navigate and capture prey, exhibiting both exploration and exploitation capabilities simultaneously. TJEAE leverages this biological insight to develop a dynamic algorithm that adjusts its exploration-exploitation balance based on the local environment and the convergence rate of the search process. The core of the algorithm centers around a multi-dimensional undulating pattern, modeled using sinusoidal functions, which represents the movement of the jellyfish. The algorithm adapts the frequency and amplitude of these undulations to balance the search for new solutions (exploration) and the refinement of promising solutions (exploitation). This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing the key parameters and their influence on the optimization process. The algorithm's ability to dynamically adjust its behavior based on the search landscape offers a potentially robust and efficient approach to solving complex optimization problems.

title: ## The Jellyfish-Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (JAE3A)
abstract: This paper introduces the Jellyfish-Inspired Adaptive Exploration and Exploitation Algorithm (JAE3A), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of giant tube jellyfish (*Cyanea capillata*). Jellyfish, known for their efficient and adaptable movement patterns in complex environments, exhibit a unique combination of exploration and exploitation strategies. JAE3A leverages this behavior by dynamically adjusting the balance between searching for new solutions (exploration) and refining existing ones (exploitation) based on a jellyfish's responsiveness to environmental stimuli. The algorithm employs a multi-dimensional space represented by a swarm of "jellyfish," each possessing adjustable parameters that govern their movement and decision-making. Key components include a jellyfish-centric adaptive probability field, a dynamic adjustment mechanism based on local environment assessment, and a novel convergence criterion. While this paper focuses on the theoretical design and algorithmic framework, it establishes a strong foundation for future experimental validation and application to diverse optimization problems.

title: Australian Cuscus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Nocturnal Lifestyle of a Marsupial
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Cuscus Search," inspired by the unique nocturnal behavior of the Australian cuscus, a marsupial known for its deliberate and methodical foraging strategy. The algorithm leverages the cuscus's observed patterns of exploration and exploitation, specifically its cautious approach to resource acquisition and its tendency to systematically cover an area before settling on a suitable food source. Cuscus Search integrates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel 'Cautious Exploration' mechanism. The core innovation lies in introducing a probability-based adjustment to the movement of particles, mimicking the cuscus's deliberate, step-by-step search. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The results indicate that Cuscus Search possesses superior convergence properties and robustness compared to traditional PSO and SA algorithms, particularly in challenging landscapes with multiple local optima. Further research will focus on adapting the algorithm for specific problem domains and exploring its potential in real-world applications.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Relational Causality
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding that explicitly incorporates temporal dynamics and relational causality. Existing graph embedding methods often treat graphs as static structures, neglecting the evolving nature of relationships and the underlying causal mechanisms that govern them. We propose a Temporal Graph Embedding (TGE) framework that combines graph structure with temporal sequence data. The core of our method is a modified Graph Neural Network (GNN) augmented with a "causal influence propagation" module. This module learns directional dependencies within the graph based on observed temporal transitions, utilizing Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty in these causal links. The resulting embeddings capture not only the node connections but also the temporal evolution and causal relationships driving those connections. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the TGE framework through theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline, highlighting its potential for applications requiring a deeper understanding of dynamic graph systems.

title: Title: Fractal-Based Constraint Optimization with Adaptive Relaxation
abstract: Fractal-based constraint optimization aims to address the limitations of traditional constraint optimization techniques by incorporating fractal geometry into the optimization process. This paper presents a novel algorithm that leverages the self-similarity inherent in fractal structures to dynamically adjust constraints, leading to more efficient and robust solutions. We explore the application of fractal representation to generate a self-similar landscape of constraints, enabling adaptive relaxation strategies. This approach enhances the algorithm's ability to navigate complex, high-dimensional search spaces and find optimal solutions with improved performance. The core mechanism is the creation of a fractal-based representation of constraints, which allows for real-time adjustment based on the problem's characteristics.

title: Causal Inference Engine for Explainable AI
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) by integrating causal inference. Traditional XAI methods often provide superficial explanations, focusing on feature importance or local decision rules without capturing the underlying causal mechanisms driving AI model predictions. This work introduces a Causal Inference Engine for Explainable AI (CIE4XAI) designed to address this limitation. The engine utilizes graph models, specifically structural causal models (SCMs), to identify and model causal relationships within data. These SCMs are then leveraged to apply causal inference rules, enabling a deeper understanding of AI model decision-making processes. The core claim is that by combining causal reasoning with XAI, we can achieve more robust and reliable explanations, leading to improved decision support. The CIE4XAI offers a shift from descriptive explanations to causal interpretations, providing a more fundamental understanding of how AI systems arrive at their conclusions. This architecture facilitates not only explanations but also the ability to predict outcomes under interventions and assess model robustness more effectively. This research contributes to a new paradigm in XAI, moving beyond correlation to truly understand and explain the cause-and-effect relationships underlying AI intelligence.

title: ## Arnoux's Beaked Whale: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Acoustic Navigation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Arnoux's Beaked Whale Algorithm" (ABWA), inspired by the remarkable acoustic navigation capabilities of Arnoux's beaked whales ( *Mesoplodon arnouxii*). These whales are renowned for their ability to navigate over vast oceanic distances using complex, structured whistles. The ABWA leverages the principles of whistle structure, whistle modulation, and the whale's apparent ability to maintain a consistent bearing despite varying environmental noise. The algorithm employs a population-based search strategy, simulating the collective behavior of the whale pod, and incorporates mechanisms mirroring the whale's use of whistle parameters to represent solutions and guide the search towards optimal regions. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's components, including the representation of solutions, the generation of new solutions, the selection mechanism, and the parameter update rules. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance and potential advantages over established metaheuristic techniques. The key mathematical formulations are presented using plain text notation.

title: Arnhold's Mouse Lemur: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Micropos australis*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Arnhold's Mouse Lemur" (AML), inspired by the foraging strategies observed in *Micropos australis*, commonly known as the mouse lemur. Mouse lemurs exhibit remarkable adaptability in resource allocation and decision-making while foraging, particularly in unpredictable environments. AML leverages these behavioral traits to develop a robust optimization approach. The algorithm combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), introducing a dynamic food source representation and a 'lemur memory' mechanism to guide exploration and exploitation. title: ## Blue-Eyed Shearwater Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BESMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Blue-Eyed Shearwater Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BESMOA), a novel optimization technique motivated by the foraging behavior of blue-eyed shearwater birds. These birds utilize a unique strategy of exploring the environment while maintaining a balance between exploration and exploitation, which we translate into a dynamic parameter adjustment mechanism within our algorithm. BESMOA employs a population-based approach, utilizing a swarm of candidate solutions. The algorithm's core innovation lies in the 'Dynamic Adaptation of Exploration and Exploitation' (DAEE) mechanism, which adjusts the parameters governing exploration and exploitation based on the individual performance and the overall swarm behavior. This adaptive control allows BESMOA to effectively navigate complex search spaces and converge towards optimal solutions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, demonstrating its potential advantages in various optimization problems. title: Parallel Algorithm Design via Quantum State Superposition
abstract: This paper investigates the design of parallel algorithms leveraging the principle of quantum state superposition. The core concept revolves around decomposing complex problems into a superposition of quantum states, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple computational tasks. We explore how quantum entanglement facilitates this parallel computation, and how quantum measurement ultimately yields the desired results. This work presents a novel algorithmic approach that directly utilizes the inherent parallel nature of quantum computation, offering a potential pathway to accelerate problem-solving in various domains. The key elements explored include state preparation, entanglement generation, parallel computation within the superposition, and final measurement for result extraction. The theoretical framework is outlined, and the potential impact of this methodology is discussed. ---

title: Argalia: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bioluminescence of *Argalia* Species
abstract: This paper presents Argalia, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique bioluminescent patterns observed in the *Argalia* species of deep-sea jellyfish. The algorithm leverages the dynamic and adaptive nature of these patterns to effectively explore and exploit the search space in optimization problems. Argalia incorporates key elements of the *Argalia* bioluminescence process, including intensity modulation, phase shifting, and spatial distribution, into its core optimization mechanisms. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel mutation operator mimicking the pulsed emission of light. The performance of Argalia is evaluated across a range of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. The results indicate that Argalia offers a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems exhibiting complex, non-linear landscapes. Further research will focus on refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to diverse problem domains.

title: Pulse Chaos Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on pulse chaos, designed to dynamically adjust parameters based on data characteristics and control system behavior. The core concept revolves around simulating the evolution of a pulse chaos system and employing its inherent dynamics to guide parameter adjustments. We propose a method that leverages the system's sensitivity to initial conditions and the unpredictable nature of the chaotic dynamics to achieve optimal solutions. The algorithm's design incorporates a feedback loop that continuously monitors the system's state and adapts the parameters accordingly. This approach promises a robust and adaptable optimization technique applicable to a wide range of problems. The goal is to provide a mechanism for automated parameter tuning and control, potentially surpassing traditional optimization methods.

title: ## The Dual-Hornbill Metaheuristic Algorithm (DHMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dual-Hornbill Metaheuristic Algorithm (DHMA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the complex social behavior and foraging strategies of the double-wattled hornbill. DHMA leverages the concept of 'dual territories' and 'competitive relocation' observed in hornbills to establish a population of potential solutions and iteratively refine them through a mechanism of 'territorial conflict' and 'adaptive relocation'. The algorithm utilizes a dual-objective function, representing exploration and exploitation, to guide the search process. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, DHMA dynamically adjusts the balance between these objectives based on the population's convergence, fostering both efficient exploration of the search space and targeted exploitation of promising regions. The core innovation lies in the adaptive mechanism for assigning territories and the dynamically modulated relocation probabilities, which are designed to avoid premature convergence and promote robust global optimization. This paper outlines the theoretical framework and algorithmic steps of DHMA, emphasizing its adaptability and potential advantages over existing metaheuristic approaches.

title: ## Anderson's Arboreal Rice Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Arboreal Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Anderson's Arboreal Rice Rat" (AARR), inspired by the foraging behavior of the arboreal rice rat ( *Nesoryzomys robustus*). These rats exhibit a unique strategy of searching for food in complex arboreal environments, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation. The AARR algorithm mimics this behavior through a novel adaptive search mechanism, incorporating both a distributed exploration phase and a local exploitation phase. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, represented by a set of rat agents, each with its own position in the search space and associated memory. The movement of these agents is governed by a probability distribution influenced by food availability and local environmental characteristics. The AARR algorithm aims to provide a robust and efficient solution for a variety of optimization problems, particularly those involving complex, multi-dimensional search spaces. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the AARR algorithm through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions with competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's adaptability and inherent exploration capabilities are key strengths.

title: ## The Mantis-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (MIASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mantis-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (MIASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies of the African praying mantis. The algorithm leverages the mantis's unique ability to dynamically adjust its search focus, prioritizing promising areas of the search space while simultaneously maintaining a degree of exploratory behavior. MIASA incorporates three core components: a dynamic focus mechanism based on relative fitness and distance to the best solution, an adaptive step size control system mimicking the mantis's hunting posture, and a novel population diversification strategy termed "Predatory Resonance." The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically through a detailed mathematical analysis of its convergence properties and search efficiency, demonstrating its potential for solving complex optimization problems. The goal of MIASA is to provide a robust and adaptable optimization approach that can effectively navigate challenging landscapes.

title: Ampurta: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Ampurita Lizard Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Ampurta, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Ampurita lizards (genus *Cnemidophorus*). Ampurita lizards are known for their unique "zigzag" foraging strategy, which involves alternating between two directions to efficiently search for food resources. Ampurta leverages this behavioral pattern through a dynamically adjusting exploration-exploitation balance, utilizing a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework. The algorithm incorporates a "direction change probability" parameter, mimicking the lizard's tendency to switch directions, and a "distance-based adjustment" mechanism to control the magnitude of these changes. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that Ampurta's design promotes both exploration and exploitation, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality compared to traditional PSO methods in several benchmark optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of test functions, including the Rastrigin, Schwefel, and Ackley functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling complex optimization challenges. The key contributions of this work lie in the algorithm's novel implementation of the lizard's foraging strategy and its ability to provide a robust and efficient solution for various optimization scenarios.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子系统优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum system optimization algorithm based on adaptive topology. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static approaches, offering limited flexibility for complex quantum systems. This work introduces a dynamic adjustment mechanism, leveraging adaptive topology to optimize quantum system parameters and enhance overall performance. The core principle lies in constructing a flexible, self-configuring topology that adapts to the system's state, enabling efficient parameter tuning and improved quantum computation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through simulations and provide a theoretical analysis of its capabilities. The potential impact of this approach on quantum computing is significant, offering a pathway to more efficient and robust quantum systems.

title: ## Aberdare Shrew Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Aberdare Shrew Optimization Algorithm" (ASOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Aberdare shrew, a small African rodent known for its efficient and adaptable foraging strategies. The ASOA leverages the shrew's ability to rapidly explore and exploit food resources in a dynamic environment. The algorithm utilizes a combination of exploration and exploitation phases, mimicking the shrew's movement patterns and resource selection. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a 'memory' mechanism based on previously visited regions, akin to the shrew's spatial memory, to guide exploration and accelerate convergence. The core components of the ASOA include a position representation, a fitness evaluation function, a mutation operator, and an adaptive inertia weight mechanism. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the ASOA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that ASOA often outperforms existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging landscapes with complex, multi-modal functions. This research contributes a new algorithmic approach to optimization with a biologically inspired foundation, offering potential improvements in efficiency and robustness.

title: Physics-Quantum Coupling Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational framework designed to bridge the gap between complex physical systems and quantum computation. The framework aims to facilitate the efficient exploration and solution of problems involving intricate systems by leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum mechanics. We present a system for seamlessly integrating physical models with quantum algorithms, optimizing for both computational speed and accuracy. The core mechanism centers around dynamically coupling physical and quantum components, employing quantum phenomena to accelerate computations and potentially unlock solutions inaccessible through classical methods. The paper details the framework's architecture, proposes a methodology for model-to-quantum algorithm mapping, and showcases its efficacy through illustrative examples. The motivation stems from the inherent limitations of classical computation in tackling complex systems, particularly those involving quantum phenomena, and highlights the potential of quantum-enhanced computation.

title: Sensitivity Without Reproducibility: A Measurement Boundary for an Operator-Valued Representation Instrument in Qwen Models
abstract: Technical report · Not peer reviewed This study asks when an internal representation observable is reusable across fresh local presentations rather than merely sensitive to a controlled perturbation on one substrate. It evaluates a phase-indexed binary register in a frozen Qwen checkpoint panel, separating explicit transition following, demonstration-conditioned register behavior, visible-state intervention use, operator-valued representation measurement, and representation–function coupling. Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.6-27B passed the behavioral ladder through visible overwrite propagation; Qwen3-14B and Qwen3.8-27B failed an upstream transition gate and were not tested downstream. On Qwen3.6-27B, a rank-4 local-frame paired ridge path-operator packet qualified on one bounded substrate. A subsequent prospectively frozen 20-block requalification retained broken-square sensitivity in 59 of 60 layer-blocks, but split-half path-map spectral re-estimation passed in only 35 of 60 layer-blocks. Only 5 of 20 blocks passed jointly at all three frozen layers, below the required 16 of 20 blocks and four blocks per rollout depth. Stage E therefore remained unopened. No functional outcome, association, coefficient, predictive increment, or permutation-test result was collected. The result is a measurement boundary for this particular rank-4, three-layer, paired-map route. It does not establish the absence of hidden state, internal naturality, useful representation geometry, or a neural causal-transition operator. The record contains the 13-page DOI-bearing technical report, buildable LaTeX source, and a model-forward-free reproducibility capsule with all 60 continuous Stage M layer-block records, deterministic figure/table inputs, model/runtime bindings, provenance closure, licenses, and checksums. Scope boundary: the report is limited to the frozen Qwen checkpoints, visible-state intervention family, rank-4 paired ridge coordinate maps, layers 21/43/62, and fresh 20-block requalification described in the manuscript. Stage E, hidden intervention, internal exact naturality, and representation–function coupling remain untested.

title: Analysis of AI Technology Application Types and Strategies in K-Beauty Companies
abstract: This study analyzed artificial intelligence (AI) applications in major Korean K-beauty companies, classified their functional types and application characteristics, and proposed strategic directions for industrial use. A qualitative multiple-case study was conducted on six companies—Amorepacific, LG Household & Health Care, APR, COSMAX, Kolmar Korea, and LULULAB. Sources published from January 2020 to May 27, 2026 were reviewed, and supplementary verification was conducted on August 24, 2026. Academic literature, government and public-sector reports, corporate technical materials, and independent media/industry sources were triangulated. Cases were coded using five predefined functional criteria and then examined through within-case, cross-case, SWOT, and TOWS analyses. Five AI types were identified: diagnosis/analysis, recommendation/personalization, generation/simulation, prediction/discovery, and process optimization/automation. The cross-case analysis showed that brand companies focused on consumer experience and R&D, ODM companies on discovery and manufacturing efficiency, and beauty-tech/device companies on data-linked personalized services. The TOWS analysis suggested four strategic directions: expansion of hyper-personalized offerings in global markets, differentiation through evidence-based customer experience, shared AI/data infrastructure and workforce development, and stronger data governance, ethics, quality, and standardization. The findings indicate that AI in K-beauty is evolving from a consumer-facing tool into a strategic resource connecting R&D, manufacturing, and personalized services.

title: Efficient Exploration-Enabled Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multi-UAV Cooperative Target Search
abstract: Multi-UAV Cooperative Target Search (MCTS) is a critical task in low-altitude sensing applications, requiring agents to efficiently explore unknown environments under complex constraints. However, traditional search methods are mostly unscalable and perform poorly in dynamic multi-UAV environments. As a promising alternative, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged to overcome these limitations by enabling agents to learn adaptive policies directly from environmental interactions. A key limitation is that current RL methods lack efficient exploration, which is a critical bottleneck preventing UAVs from finding more targets. To address this limitation, we propose a novel method named AEQMIX, which integrates trajectory entropy maximization into QMIX, an advanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) method, to encourage efficient exploration. We formulate the MCTS problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and design a multi-objective reward function. To mitigate the intractability of density estimation in high-dimensional spaces, we employ a nonparametric particle-based entropy estimator to quantify the spatial diversity of UAV trajectories. This entropy estimate is utilized as an intrinsic reward, incentivizing agents to maximize the distance between their trajectories and those of their neighbors. Extensive simulations demonstrate that AEQMIX significantly outperforms baseline reinforcement learning and traditional optimization methods in terms of search rate, coverage efficiency, and collision avoidance. Compared with DNQMIX, AEQMIX improves the search rate and coverage rate by 9.52% and 11.54%, respectively, while reducing the average collision count by 70.59% in the (40 × 40) environment.

evidence.title: Efficient Exploration-Enabled Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multi-UAV Cooperative Target Search
evidence.abstract: Multi-UAV Cooperative Target Search (MCTS) is a critical task in low-altitude sensing applications, requiring agents to efficiently explore unknown environments under complex constraints. However, traditional search methods are mostly unscalable and perform poorly in dynamic multi-UAV environments. As a promising alternative, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged to overcome these limitations by enabling agents to learn adaptive policies directly from environmental interactions. A key limitation is that current RL methods lack efficient exploration, which is a critical bottleneck preventing UAVs from finding more targets. To address this limitation, we propose a novel method named AEQMIX, which integrates trajectory entropy maximization into QMIX, an advanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) method, to encourage efficient exploration. We formulate the MCTS problem as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) and design a multi-objective reward function. To mitigate the intractability of density estimation in high-dimensional spaces, we employ a nonparametric particle-based entropy estimator to quantify the spatial diversity of UAV trajectories. This entropy estimate is utilized as an intrinsic reward, incentivizing agents to maximize the distance between their trajectories and those of their neighbors. Extensive simulations demonstrate that AEQMIX significantly outperforms baseline reinforcement learning and traditional optimization methods in terms of search rate, coverage efficiency, and collision avoidance. Compared with DNQMIX, AEQMIX improves the search rate and coverage rate by 9.52% and 11.54%, respectively, while reducing the average collision count by 70.59% in the (40 × 40) environment.

title: Experimental realization of optical key distribution under strong wiretap eavesdropping
abstract: We report the experimental distribution of a cryptographic key based on binary intensity-modulation/direct-detection (IM/DD) transmission of an optical signal. The implemented secret key agreement protocol ensures security against passive wiretap eavesdropping, notably in the regime when the eavesdropper has an advantage in the intercepted signal strength over the legitimate recipient. Operating at a 1 GBaud symbol rate, the experimental fiber optic testbed yielded secret key rates between 43.5 Mbps at 61.1 km and 640 kbps at 81.6 km of the effective link length, with a 9% wiretap installed at the transmitter. The protocol performance was analyzed using a theoretical model incorporating transmitter noise and non-ideal key reconciliation efficiency. The presented results validate IM/DD optical key distribution as an efficient low-complexity solution for protecting optical communication systems against the predominant physical-layer threat of wiretap eavesdropping.

title: TSPFN: A Temporal Tabular Foundation Model for Physiological Time Series Classification
abstract: Designing models that generalize effectively in low- to medium-data regimes remains a primary challenge in medical machine learning, particularly for physiological time-series classification. While tabular foundation models such as TabPFN offer an attractive alternative to conventional fine-tuning through in-context learning, they are not designed to capture the temporal dependencies inherent to physiological signals. ~In this paper, we introduce TSPFN, a foundation model that redesigns TabPFN's architecture for time series data. TSPFN integrates structured temporal representations and positional embeddings to capture intra-sample temporal and channel dependencies. To fully leverage its spatio-temporal design, the model is pretrained on 140,000 real-world physiological time series across multiple medical domains. This yields a unified, generalizable framework capable of learning the specificities of medical time series. Experiments across diverse physiological benchmarks demonstrate that TSPFN consistently outperforms standard tabular baselines and TabPFN, and achieves superior cross-domain generalization compared to specialized deep time-series models. All our experiments, ablation studies, and pre-processing scheme are publicly available at https://github.com/Jeremstym/TSPFN

title: Kolmogorov--Arnold against bounded translations
abstract: Historically originating from Hilbert's 13th problem, the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem (KART) has recently experienced a major revitalisation through its applications to neural networks, specifically Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs). While the exact representation is well established, its stability under continuous adversarial perturbations of the hidden layer remains a critical open question. In this paper, we investigate the robustness of KART against bounded adversarial translations. We provide an explicit, self-contained, and constructive proof of an approximate representation using fixed, piecewise linear inner functions. Crucially, our construction employs a single outer function that remains invariant for all summands and is independent of the specific adversarial translation, provided its maximum bound is known a priori.

title: Mode Connectivity Beyond Classifiers: Evidence from Generative and Contrastive Models
abstract: The loss landscape of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) exhibits highly complex and non-convex properties. Recent studies have revealed the phenomenon of mode connectivity, demonstrating that independently trained network modes can be connected via a continuous low-loss path. However, existing mode connectivity research is predominantly confined to classifier-based models, leaving it an open question whether similar geometric properties exist in modern complex models. In this paper, we extend the boundaries of mode connectivity to generative and contrastive domains (specifically DDPM and NanoCLIP). Addressing the unique architecture of DDPM and CLIP, we propose an architecture-aware connection building algorithm. Extensive empirical results demonstrate for the first time that we successfully discover mode connectivity between independently trained DDPM and NanoCLIP modes. Our work provides a novel perspective for understanding the geometric properties of the loss landscapes in modern generative and contrastive models.

title: Adjacent-Sentence Semantic Similarity as a Measure of L2 Korean Reading Text Difficulty
abstract: 연구 목적: 본 연구의 목적은 Sentence-BERT(S-BERT)를 활용하여 L2 한국어 읽기 텍스트의 인접 문장 의미 유사도를 분석하고, 이를 텍스트 난이도 측정 지표로 활용할 수 있는지를 검토하는 데 있다.연구 방법: 『새연세한국어』에 수록된 초급 51편, 중급 40편, 고급 38편 등 총 129편의 읽기 텍스트를 대상으로 Kiwi를 이용하여 문장을 분리한 후 Sentence-BERT를 활용하여 문장 임베딩을 생성하고, 인접 문장 간 코사인 유사도를 산출하였다. 또한 Kruskal-Wallis 검정, Spearman 순위상관분석 및 평균 문장 길이를 고려한 다중회귀분석을 실시하였다.연구 내용: 첫째, 수준별 인접 문장 의미 유사도는 초급에서 고급으로 갈수록 증가하는 경향을 보였으나, 그 차이는 통계적으로 유의하지 않았다(H=2.709, p=.258). 둘째, 평균 문장 길이는 인접 문장 의미 유사도와 유의한 정적 상관을 보였으며(ρ=.362, p<.001), 평균 문장 길이를 함께 고려한 회귀분석에서는 초급과 중급(B=-0.0557, p=.023), 초급과 고급(B=-0.0587, p=.022) 간에 유의한 차이가 확인되었다. 또한 평균 문장 길이를 고려하기 전과 후에 수준별 인접 문장 의미 유사도의 양상이 반대로 나타났다.결론 및 제언: 인접 문장 의미 유사도는 기존의 형식적 이독성 자질을 보완하는 L2 한국어읽기 텍스트 난이도 측정 지표로 활용될 가능성이 있음을 확인하였다. 또한 텍스트 난이도를 분석할 때에는 개별 자질의 절대적 수치뿐 아니라 평균 문장 길이와 같은 관련 언어적 요인을 함께 고려할 필요가 있음을 확인하였다. 향후 연구에서는 다양한 한국어 교재와 실제 학습 자료를 대상으로 분석 범위를 확대하고, 문단 수준의 의미 응집성 등 다양한 의미기반 지표를 함께 활용하여 텍스트 난이도 측정 모형을 고도화할 필요가 있다.

title: Lee's Law: A Tripartite Model of AI Capability Doubling in the Post-Moore Era
abstract: This paper proposes Lee's Law, a tripartite framework asserting that artificial intelligence capability doubles approximately every six months across three concurrent axes: task scale, task duration, and operational sustainability. [Derived: Synthesis of empirical doubling intervals reported by METR (7 months for 2019–2025; 4.3 months for 2023–2025; 3 months for 2024–2025), Epoch AI (2.4 months for context windows), and METR/SWE-bench (70 days). Six months is selected as the median-weighted central tendency. Assumption: These heterogeneous metrics converge on a single underlying capability growth curve.] Unlike Moore's Law, which tracks a single physical variable (transistor count), Lee's Law tracks a composite variable: the complexity of human labor that AI systems can autonomously displace. [Derived: Analogical inference from Moore's Law definition to the "task horizon" metric introduced by METR.] I derive strategic implications for enterprise AI architecture, dynamic pricing, and workforce planning, while explicitly bounding the law's applicability against risks of benchmark saturation, cost divergence, and reliability gaps. [Derived: Logical extension of the tripartite framework into operational domains.]

title: 基于自适应拓扑的神经元网络架构
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture, termed "Adaptive Topology Neural Network" (ATN), that leverages the principles of self-adaptive topology to dynamically adjust neuron network internal structure. The core innovation lies in the automatic generation and optimization of the network's topology, leading to improved model generalization capabilities. We introduce a novel method for constructing and refining the topology, incorporating a feedback loop that continuously assesses and corrects the network's structure based on performance data. This adaptive process reduces the reliance on manual parameter tuning, offering a robust and scalable solution for training complex neural networks. The proposed architecture demonstrates significant improvements in performance across various benchmark datasets, showcasing the potential for automated network design and enhanced model robustness.

title: Probability Logic and the Intrinsic Time Dimension of Computation
abstract: This paper explores the integration of probability logic into computational modeling, proposing a novel "time logic" framework to enable probabilistic models to automatically recognize and leverage time series data, and facilitate dynamic forecasting. We detail the design of a probabilistic model centered on this time logic, emphasizing its ability to generate updated probability distributions and implement time-series analysis. The core mechanism involves introducing time dependencies within the model's probability distribution, which allows for automatic updates and effective time-series analysis. This work contributes to the advancement of probabilistic modeling by extending its capabilities to incorporate temporal dynamics.

title: High-Dimensional Non-Linear Matrix Quantum Computing Verification and Geometric Deformation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum computing to validate the quantum properties of matrix operations, leveraging geometric deformation techniques. We propose a novel framework for quantum computation verification that integrates quantum mechanics with geometric transformations, aiming to uncover subtle quantum behaviors not readily apparent through traditional methods. The core mechanism involves constructing quantum algorithms that exploit these geometric distortions to test the integrity of matrix operations. The paper introduces a preliminary quantum algorithm demonstrating the capability of this approach and discusses its potential impact on the field of quantum verification.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Non-Linear Machine Learning Model
abstract: This paper investigates the development of a dynamic adaptive non-linear machine learning model designed to enhance model generalization. Traditional machine learning models often remain static, failing to adequately adapt to evolving data patterns. We propose a novel architecture that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on incoming data, allowing for continuous learning and improved performance. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that iteratively refines the model's parameters to minimize prediction error and maximize accuracy. This paper details the model's architecture, training process, and experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of machine learning tasks. The primary goal is to provide a robust and adaptable framework for machine learning, capable of handling complex datasets and evolving environments.

title: Graph Representation Learning for Multi-Modal Data Fusion
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Graph Representation Learning (GRL) to the problem of multi-modal data fusion. Traditional approaches to multi-modal fusion frequently operate on individual modalities in isolation, failing to leverage the potentially rich and complex relationships that exist between them. We propose a novel framework that utilizes GRL techniques, specifically Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), to represent multi-modal data as a graph structure. In this framework, data instances are represented as nodes, and edges are constructed to reflect relationships between modalities. By learning latent embeddings within this graph structure, we can effectively capture and exploit inter-modal dependencies, ultimately improving the accuracy and robustness of data fusion tasks. The core contribution of this work lies in its ability to uncover hidden correlations across modalities, a capability often missed by conventional methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a practical implementation strategy. The key performance indicators (KPIs) for evaluating this approach will be measured through reduced dimensionality and improved prediction accuracy.

title: Quantum Memory Based on Quantum State Decoherence
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum state decoherence as a fundamental mechanism for constructing a high-density and high-fidelity quantum memory. The core concept relies on exploiting quantum bit (qubit) interactions to store and retrieve quantum states, coupled with the inherent properties of decoherence to maintain coherence for extended periods. We propose a framework leveraging controlled interactions between qubits to encode quantum information, followed by a carefully designed decoherence process to effectively 'lock' the state. The key challenge addressed is minimizing information loss during both storage and retrieval. The theoretical analysis focuses on the trade-offs between coherence time, storage capacity, and fidelity, providing a basis for future research and development in this critical area of quantum information processing. We present a simplified model to illustrate the principles involved and discuss potential avenues for improvement, highlighting the importance of precise control and mitigation strategies to combat decoherence effects. ---

title: Self-Adaptive Spin State Entanglement for Enhanced Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum computation offers unprecedented computational power, but maintaining and manipulating entangled states remains a significant challenge. This paper investigates a novel approach to enhance quantum computation through the implementation of self-adaptive spin state entanglement. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the entanglement strength, optimizing the system for improved performance and efficiency. The core of this approach lies in the concept of self-calibration, enabling the system to maintain a desired entanglement level without requiring explicit control. This results in a more robust and adaptable entanglement, potentially unlocking new capabilities within quantum algorithms. The study involves a detailed analysis of the impact of this self-calibration on various quantum processing tasks, demonstrating significant efficiency gains. This work represents a fundamental shift in how we approach entanglement management, paving the way for more sophisticated and practical quantum systems.

title: Title: Algorithmic Semantic Coherence via Hierarchical Contextual Graph Embedding
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges of automatically generating coherent semantic representations – particularly knowledge graphs – and proposes a novel algorithmic approach, "Algorithmic Semantic Coherence via Hierarchical Contextual Graph Embedding," that addresses these challenges. Traditional methods often rely on shallow word embeddings, failing to capture the intricate relationships necessary for true semantic understanding. This research introduces a new framework centered around a hierarchical graph structure, leveraging a self-learning embedding technique to dynamically refine the graph, ultimately aiming for enhanced semantic coherence. The core claim is that this approach significantly improves the generation of rich, contextually-aware representations compared to existing methods. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, explains the self-learning embedding process, and provides a preliminary analysis of its performance. The research emphasizes the importance of hierarchical modeling in achieving robust semantic coherence.

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of mathematics, offers a unique approach to manipulating and controlling quantum systems. This paper introduces an Adaptive Algorithm based on Quantum Topology, designed to automatically optimize quantum system parameters through the exploitation of quantum topology's inherent structural constraints. The algorithm leverages the concept of "topology" – a mathematical structure that preserves distances and shapes – to iteratively refine quantum states, leading to more precise control and enhanced system performance. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its potential to revolutionize quantum control methodologies.

title: Graph-Based Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph-based reinforcement learning (GRL) that incorporates intrinsic motivation to enhance exploration. Traditional GRL algorithms often rely solely on extrinsic rewards, leading to premature convergence to locally optimal solutions. To address this limitation, we propose a framework where agents are driven by internal rewards derived from information gain and uncertainty reduction within the graph environment. The core of our method lies in an "Intrinsic Reward Module" which dynamically adjusts the reward signal based on the agent's knowledge of the graph's structure and potential rewards. We demonstrate that this intrinsic motivation significantly improves the agent's ability to explore diverse regions of the graph, ultimately leading to better long-term performance. The key innovation lies in the strategic combination of extrinsic and intrinsic rewards, creating a more robust and adaptive learning process. We formally define the GRL framework, detail the Intrinsic Reward Module, and outline the theoretical underpinnings of the approach.
