title: Ouroboros: Self-Referential Backdoor Attacks on Speech Enhancement via Clean Audio Triggers
abstract: Speech enhancement models are widely deployed as frontend modules in real-time speech services, yet their vulnerability to backdoor attacks remains unexplored. Existing backdoor methods are confined to classification tasks and rely on active trigger injection, an assumption incompatible with the passive processing nature of speech enhancement models. In this paper, we propose Ouroboros, a novel backdoor attack framework that leverages the ideal clean outputs of speech enhancement models as natural triggers, enabling inference-time activation without any external trigger injection. Extensive evaluations show Ouroboros achieves near-perfect attack success rates with minimal performance degradation on diverse models and datasets. Physical-world validations confirm that naturally recorded, unaltered clean audio can reliably activate the backdoor. Moreover, Ouroboros generalizes to targeted content-tampering attacks and remains effective against common filtering and finetuning defenses.

In this paper, we propose Ouroboros, a novel backdoor attack framework that leverages the ideal clean outputs of speech enhancement models as natural triggers, enabling inference-time activation without any external trigger injection. Extensive evaluations show Ouroboros achieves near-perfect attack success rates with minimal performance degradation on diverse models and datasets. Physical-world validations confirm that naturally recorded, unaltered clean audio can reliably activate the backdoor. Moreover, Ouroboros generalizes to targeted content-tampering attacks and remains effective against common filtering and finetuning defenses.

title: A Comparative Study of Korean Morphological Analyzers for Non-standard Forms in L2 Korean Writing
abstract: 연구 목적: 본 연구는 초급 한국어 학습자 작문의 자동 쓰기 평가에 적합한 형태소 분석기를 탐색하고 비정형 표현의 처리에서 나타나는 분석기별 차이를 살펴보는 것을 목적으로 하였다.연구 방법: 개발 언어 및 호환성, 품사 태그셋, 처리 속도, 사용자 사전 관리 용이성의 네 기준을 설정하고 Kiwi, KOMORAN, Okt, Kkma의 분석 결과를 비교하였다. 또한 초급 한국어 학습자 10명의 작문에서 비정형성이 두드러진 8개 어절을 추출하여 네 분석기의 형태소 분절 및 품사 태깅 결과를 비교하였다.연구 내용: 첫째, Kiwi는 오타 교정 모드를 통해 일부 단순 오탈자를 부분적으로 교정하였으며 띄어쓰기 오류가 포함된 표현에서도 상대적으로 안정적인 분절 결과를 보였다. 둘째, KOMORAN은 분석이 어려운 입력을 NA로 처리하는 경향이 있었고, Okt는 비정형 어절을 하나의 단위로 처리하는 사례가 나타났으며 Kkma는 일부 사례에서 과분절 양상을 보였다. 셋째, 자모 분리 오류나 목표형과의 거리가 큰 심각한 오탈자는 네 분석기 모두 안정적으로 복원하지 못하였다.결론 및 제언: 분석 결과, 초급 학습자 작문의 자동 쓰기 평가에는 Kiwi가 비교 대상 중 상대적으로 안정적인 분석기로 판단되었다. 다만 심각한 오탈자와 자모 분리 오류를 처리하기 위해서는 형태소 분석 이전 단계의 별도 전처리 절차가 필요하다. 후속 연구에서는 더 많은 학습자 작문과 다양한 오류 유형을 대상으로 분석기별 처리 성능을 검증하고, 형태소분석 오류가 자동 쓰기 평가 자질과 최종 평가 결과의 신뢰도에 미치는 영향을 살펴볼 필요가 있다.

title: A Systematic Review of Relation Extraction for various Indian and Non-Indian Languages
abstract: Abstract This article comprehensively reviews text relation extraction for various Indian and non-Indian languages. The study involves a comparative investigation of diverse models developed using machine learning (ML) & deep learning (DL) approach for relation extraction. A detailed literature review has been conducted for diverse Indian and non-Indian languages. The comparative study focuses on the effectiveness of diverse models across these languages. This paper highlights the strengths and limitations of various approaches, providing insights into the best practices for relation extraction in diverse linguistic contexts.

title: Governed Context Compression: Measured Abstention as a First-Class Property
abstract: Context compressors are evaluated on how much they remove. We argue and measure a prior question: what a compressor should be allowed to touch. TekMyra is a compression router: content is classified and routed to codecs under a safety contract with locked-span preservation, refusal as a first-class outcome, and verification before emission. Before anything is emitted, a verifier confirms that every locked span (an account number, a citation, a monetary amount) is represented exactly once in the output; if the check fails, the compressor retries on a safer route, and if the retry fails too, it emits nothing. On the public corpus we report a headline of 62.1458% effective byte reduction over 138 externally sourced fixtures, with the 6 refusals stated beside it (4.35% of fixtures, 3.55% of bytes, contributing zero saving); per-cell figures on honest denominators; and pre-registered comparisons against LLMLingua-2 in which the context-window asymmetry was declared before any result existed. Both bases are printed because they disagree mechanistically: LLMLingua-2 leads on cl100k token reduction (62.6016% vs 58.1101%) while TekMyra leads on effective byte reduction (62.1458% vs 61.4640%), the byte basis committed as our headline denominator before any comparison figure existed; handed our span map, their preservation exceeds ours, a pre-registered flip condition published as triggered. On the shipped benchmark corpora we report reached-set ratios of 0.7409 on synthetic (28 of 28 reached, 0 refused) and 0.2929 on long_context_v1 (26 of 40 reached, 14 refused, counted at zero saving in the corpus token figure). What remains ours by measurement: the span map, refusal accounting, and fail-closed verification. One limitation is stated up front: the trained artifacts every headline rate requires ship as a separate release asset, and a clean checkout of the repository measures a no-op compressor.

title: Reader Surplus Separating Source Structure from the Structure of Reading
abstract: Reader Surplus Separating Source Structure from the Structure of Reading Dean Kulik QuHarmonics Research Group · ORCID 0009-0003-3128-8828 August 2026 Abstract Measurement theory is well supplied with accounts of what happens when a reader has too little resolution for its source. Aliasing, coarse-graining, and information loss are all instances, and all describe the same failure: distinctions present in the source collapse onto a single observation. This paper concerns the opposite failure, which is less discussed and considerably more dangerous, because it produces output rather than silence. When a reader imposes more address structure than its source supports, the surplus does not vanish. It appears in the record, and it appears as structure — correlated, reproducible, and mathematically consistent. Nothing marks it as the reader's own. A sinusoid sampled at ten times the necessary rate yields ten times the data and not one additional distinction; the added samples carry adjacent-sample correlation rising to 0.99998, which is a measurement of the sampling grid rather than of the signal. The clean geometric case is a sphere under a latitude-longitude chart. The unmarked sphere has a transitive symmetry group and therefore no distinguished point: its quotient under the rotation group is a single point, so it supports no intrinsic address whatever. A chart supplies two dimensions of address regardless, and that surplus cannot be sustained everywhere. At the poles every longitude terminates at one location, so the source offers one place while the representation offers a continuum of labels. The sphere is perfectly regular there. The chart is not. Regular source, singular representation, and the singularity belongs entirely to the reading. Two audit rules follow and they are mirror images. A reader may not claim distinctions it cannot resolve; and a reader may not attribute its own surplus structure to the source. Existing verification discipline enforces the first and has no test for the second. Applied retroactively to a body of work by this author, the second rule identifies six independent retracted claims as a single failure class rather than six unrelated errors. The paper closes with the bound. A source can be re-addressed without disturbance exactly within the commutant of its own evolution, which is the entire operator algebra when the source is static and shrinks as the source does more. A file admits six mutually incompatible partitions and survives all of them byte-identically because it holds still. That is not an engineering achievement. It is the price. Contents 1. An asymmetry in the standard account Ask what goes wrong when an instrument is inadequate to its subject and the literature answers immediately. The Nyquist–Shannon theorem gives the threshold below which frequency components become indistinguishable. Coarse-graining, partial traces, projections, and lossy compression all describe the same structure: a many-to-one map from source states to observations, with a fibre of states the reader cannot separate. Ask what goes wrong when an instrument exceeds its subject and the question sounds odd. More resolution is assumed harmless. Take more samples, use more coordinates, refine the mesh — the worst case is redundancy, and redundancy is merely wasteful. That assumption is wrong, and the error it permits is worse than the one it guards against. Insufficient resolution produces silence: distinctions that were present do not appear. Excess resolution produces speech. The surplus enters the record as structure, and structure invites explanation. An under-resolved reading fails to report what is there. An over-resolved reading reports what is not. The second failure is harder to detect because its output is well-behaved. Oversampled data is not noisy; it is smooth, correlated, and reproducible. Repeat the measurement and the same surplus appears. Every internal consistency check passes, because the surplus is genuinely consistent — with the reader. 1.1 What this paper establishes The reader–source relation has three regimes, not two, and the third has no standard name. Surplus is measurable: the diagnostic is whether added reader structure yields source-invariant distinctions. The sphere under a spherical chart is the exact case, with the pole singularity belonging demonstrably to the chart and not to the sphere. Two mirror audit rules cover both failures, where existing discipline covers one. Applied to a real body of work, the second rule collapses six independent retractions into one failure class. Surplus addressing is free exactly when the source is static, and the bound is the commutant of the source's own evolution. 2. The axis Write the reading as a map from source states to observations: rho : X -> Y Two quantities govern its behaviour. The source supports some number of independent distinctions, call it S. The reader imposes some number of independent addresses, call it Q. The regimes follow from their relation and not from either alone. Regime Condition What the fibre does What appears in the record Deficit Q < S many source states share one observation less than is there Matched Q \u2248 S the map is near-injective what is there Surplus Q > S many addresses share one source distinction more than is there The deficit and surplus fibres run in opposite directions and this is the structural point. In deficit, the fibre lives in the source: several states collapse to one reading. In surplus, the fibre lives in the reader: several addresses describe one source distinction. Both are many-to-one; they differ in which side is many. Resolution as ordinarily used is a property of the reader alone, and a one-dimensional quantity. It cannot express either failure, because both are relations. A reader is not too coarse or too fine in itself; it is too coarse or too fine for a particular source. 3. Deficit, measured The familiar side is included because the surplus side is only legible against it, and because the same experiment run in one direction gives both. Construct a source with twelve distinct frequency components at 50, 130, 270, 410, 530, 670, 790, 910, 1030, 1150, 1270 and 1390 Hz. Sample at a falling rate and count how many observed frequencies remain distinct — two components collide when they alias to the same position in the observed band. Sample rate (Hz) Nyquist Distinct addresses Collapsed Reads as 4000 2000 12 0 resolved 2000 1000 12 0 resolved 1000 500 11 1 partly folded 600 300 7 5 partly folded 400 200 7 5 partly folded 300 150 6 6 partly folded 200 100 5 7 partly folded 120 60 3 9 smooth 60 30 2 10 smooth 20 10 1 11 smooth Twelve distinctions become one. The components did not leave the source: raise the rate and all twelve return, undamaged, in their original positions. What changed was the observation map, which became progressively many-to-one. Smoothness in this experiment is not an absence of structure. It is a large fibre. This licenses a precise use of a phrase that is otherwise loose. Saying information was lost is misleading, because nothing in the source changed and nothing had to be reconstructed. The accurate statement is that mathematical distinctions became inaccessible through that particular map. The mathematics remained in the source and the interface stopped reaching it. 4. Surplus, measured Now run the same axis upward. Take a source with exactly two components, at 17 Hz and 50 Hz, and sample it far above the rate its bandwidth requires. Sample rate (Hz) Samples Adjacent-sample correlation Independent components 200 200 0.173248 2 1000 1000 0.959806 2 5000 5000 0.998377 2 50000 50000 0.999984 2 Two hundred and fifty times the samples. Zero additional source distinctions. And the adjacent-sample correlation climbs to 0.999984, which is a strong, stable, reproducible measurement — of the sampling grid. This is the danger stated concretely. The correlation is real, it survives repetition, it is not noise, and every consistency check on it passes. A reader who did not know the source had two components would find a highly structured record and would be right about its structure. The structure would be the reader's own. 4.1 The diagnostic The test that separates the two cases is not a property of a single reading. It is a comparison between readings at different reader capacities: Increase the reader's structure. Do source-invariant distinctions increase? If yes, the added capacity uncovered source structure — the fibre split, and the split is reproducible across independent readings of the same source. If no, the added capacity produced description without distinction, and the surplus belongs to the reader. In the deficit experiment, raising the rate from 20 Hz to 4000 Hz took the distinguishable count from 1 to 12. Source structure was uncovered. In the surplus experiment, raising the rate from 200 Hz to 50000 Hz took the count from 2 to 2. Nothing was uncovered, and what grew was correlation, which is a measure of the grid's own fineness. The diagnostic requires two readings. This is not incidental: a single reading, however careful, cannot distinguish source structure from reader structure, because both appear in it identically. 5. The exact case: regular source, singular representation Geometry supplies an instance where both sides can be computed rather than estimated, and where the surplus is not approximately identifiable but exactly locatable. 5.1 The source has no address The rotation group acts transitively on a sphere: for any two surface poin

title: Title: Quantum Adaptive Probability System Modeling
abstract: Quantum adaptive probability system modeling aims to develop a novel approach to modeling quantum systems by leveraging quantum self-adaptability. This research explores the application of quantum self-adaptability to enhance system stability and accelerate quantum computation. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts system parameters based on internal quantum states, thereby mitigating inherent instability issues commonly encountered in quantum systems. This model will provide a significant advancement in the design and management of quantum algorithms, potentially offering improved performance and robustness. title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Commonsense Knowledge Acquisition
abstract: Current artificial intelligence systems, particularly deep learning models, often exhibit a significant lack of commonsense knowledge – the implicit understanding of the world that humans possess effortlessly. This deficiency limits their ability to reason effectively in novel situations and to generalize learning across diverse contexts. This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge acquisition called Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning, which aims to bridge the gap between the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks and the structured reasoning abilities of symbolic systems. The core idea is to integrate these two paradigms, allowing neural networks to learn complex patterns from raw data and subsequently translate these patterns into formal logical rules. This facilitates a more robust and adaptable knowledge acquisition system, capable of handling ambiguous and uncertain information. The proposed framework leverages neural networks for data representation and feature extraction, while symbolic reasoning engines provide a mechanism for logical inference and rule generation. We outline the key components of this system and discuss its potential benefits and challenges. This approach addresses the limitations of existing AI systems by combining the strengths of both neural networks and symbolic reasoning, ultimately leading to a more intelligent and versatile knowledge base.

title: Adaptive Differential Privacy with Personalized Noise Calibration
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to differential privacy, Adaptive Differential Privacy (ADP), designed to mitigate the drawbacks of traditional uniform noise addition. The core challenge in applying differential privacy lies in balancing privacy protection with data utility. Standard differential privacy utilizes a fixed noise scale, often leading to excessive noise for certain queries, thereby significantly reducing data utility. ADP addresses this by implementing a personalized noise calibration strategy. This strategy dynamically adjusts the noise level based on three key factors: the individual's data sensitivity (derived from statistical properties of their data), the complexity of the query being executed, and the desired level of data utility. The system employs a feedback loop to continuously monitor and refine the noise level, optimizing the trade-off between privacy and utility. We demonstrate the potential of ADP to significantly improve data utility compared to standard differential privacy, particularly in scenarios with heterogeneous data and complex queries. The presented framework provides a flexible and adaptive solution for achieving strong differential privacy guarantees while maximizing the value derived from sensitive datasets.

title: ## Azorean Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ABMOA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Azorean Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ABMOA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Azorean bat. Bats utilize a sophisticated echolocation strategy to locate prey in complex environments. This algorithm leverages key aspects of bat echolocation, including pulse emission, frequency modulation, and receiver sensitivity, to guide the search process. ABMOA employs a population-based approach, mimicking the bat's social foraging dynamics. The algorithm incorporates a novel parameter, the "Echo Strength," which dynamically adjusts the exploration and exploitation balance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ABMOA on a selection of benchmark optimization problems, highlighting its ability to converge to near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational effort. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results suggest that ABMOA offers a competitive alternative, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multimodal solutions. The core of ABMOA lies in its adaptation of bat-inspired principles for efficient and robust optimization.

title: Dynamic Topological Semantic Learning (DTSL)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topological Semantic Learning (DTSL), a novel approach to semantic understanding based on interactive observation and dynamic topological graph construction. The core claim of DTSL is that a system can automatically learn and build semantic relationships between objects by observing and simulating their interactions, dynamically adjusting its topology to reflect these evolving relationships. DTSL leverages a combination of reinforcement learning and graph neural networks to achieve this. The system begins with an unstructured graph and utilizes observation units (e.g., visual sensors, text analyzers) to collect data on object interactions. A reinforcement learning agent then iteratively modifies the graph's connections – adding or removing edges – to maximize performance on specified tasks, such as relationship prediction or instruction execution. A graph neural network (GNN) represents and reasons about the graph structure, guiding the connection adjustments. Over time, DTSL constructs a dynamic topology that directly reflects the semantic relationships within the observed environment. This approach contrasts with traditional methods relying on pre-defined knowledge graphs or manually annotated semantic relations, offering a more adaptive and flexible solution.

The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for application in various fields. The key contributions of this work include the development of a novel algorithm design, a unique representation of the search space, and a dynamic parameter adaptation strategy, all inspired by the intelligent foraging behavior of the Asian red-cheeked squirrel. title: Quantum Information Storage and Retrieval: Topological Optimization
abstract: Quantum information storage and retrieval represent a significant challenge and opportunity for advancing quantum technology. Traditional methods often focus on the physical properties of qubits, while a novel approach – topological optimization – offers the potential to dramatically enhance both storage and retrieval efficiency while simultaneously bolstering security. This paper explores the application of topological optimization principles to quantum information systems, focusing on the design of novel qubit architectures and retrieval algorithms that leverage the inherent robustness of topological states. We investigate how manipulating the topology of a qubit system can fundamentally alter its performance, leading to substantial improvements in both data density and error correction capabilities. The research delves into specific optimization strategies, including the creation of topological circuits and the implementation of adaptive error mitigation techniques. The ultimate goal is to establish a framework for quantum information storage and retrieval systems that are both highly reliable and computationally efficient.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Topological Network Self-Organization
abstract: This paper investigates the self-organization of dynamic quantum entanglement topological networks. The core claim is to leverage the dynamic nature of topological entanglement to enable adaptive topological rearrangement among quantum network nodes, ultimately optimizing quantum information transmission efficiency and resilience. The proposed mechanism utilizes a topological sensitivity mapping based on quantum entanglement, combined with machine learning algorithms to predict network topology changes and control adjustments to entangled states between nodes for self-organization. We demonstrate a novel approach to constructing quantum networks with enhanced adaptability and performance compared to traditional static topological designs. The key mathematical framework is presented, focusing on entanglement quantification, network topology representation, and the optimization algorithms used for self-organization. The research addresses a critical gap in current topological quantum network design by introducing a dynamic, self-adaptive system. The results suggest significant potential for future quantum network architectures, particularly in scenarios demanding high bandwidth, robustness, and scalability.

abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols leveraging the principles of quantum coherence draining. The research addresses the need for improved QKD performance and robust security by exploring novel approaches to managing decoherence, a significant limitation in current QKD implementations. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of coherence draining's potential role in shaping more effective and secure quantum communication systems. The core objective is to demonstrate a quantifiable improvement in key generation rate and security margins through strategic application of coherence draining techniques. ---

title: ## Mimic Crab Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (MCIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimic Crab Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (MCIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm motivated by the foraging behavior of mimic crabs. These crabs exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between exploratory and exploitative movements, adapting their search strategy based on the density of food sources. MCIMO leverages this behavior through a dynamic probability distribution and adaptive movement strategy. The algorithm employs a population of potential solutions, where each solution's position is represented as a vector (s_1, s_2, ..., s_K). A core element of MCIMO is the "Crab Density Estimation" function, which assesses the concentration of promising solutions in the search space. This function dynamically adjusts the probability of exploratory versus exploitative movements, guiding the population towards areas with higher potential. MCIMO's performance is evaluated through its adaptive parameters, including the exploration probability (e_p), exploitation probability (e_x), and crab density threshold (C_t). The algorithm's design aims to efficiently navigate complex search spaces while avoiding premature convergence, inspired by the mimic crab's resilience and adaptability in challenging environments.

title: ## The African Land Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ALS-MHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the African Land Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ALS-MHOA), a novel optimization method derived from the foraging behavior of *Achatina fulica*, a large terrestrial snail found in Africa. The algorithm mimics the snail's exploratory movement, adaptive feeding strategy, and response to environmental changes. ALS-MHOA utilizes a segmented search space, representing the snail's territory, and employs a "pheromone trail" mechanism inspired by the snail's scent marking to guide exploration and exploitation. The core of the algorithm involves a dynamic territory segmentation, a probabilistic feeding strategy based on environmental cues, and an adaptive trail reinforcement system. This approach offers a potentially robust and efficient method for tackling complex optimization problems, particularly those with high dimensionality and non-convex landscapes. The algorithm's parameters are designed to reflect the snail's inherent adaptive capabilities, aiming for a balance between exploration and exploitation. This paper outlines the theoretical framework, the key components, and the underlying principles of ALS-MHOA, laying the groundwork for future experimental validation and application.

title: European Garden Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ESG-MHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the European Garden Snail-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ESG-MHOA), drawing inspiration from the foraging behavior of European garden snails. The algorithm mimics the snail's exploration and exploitation strategies, utilizing a layered approach to navigate a search space. The core of ESG-MHOA lies in a dynamically adjusted 'shell' representation, where each snail's position within the shell is determined by a combination of global and local search parameters. The algorithm incorporates a novel 'feeding' mechanism that influences the movement of snails, promoting diversification and preventing premature convergence. Furthermore, a 'mud' layer is introduced to simulate the snail's environment, introducing stochasticity and guiding the search towards promising regions. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, highlighting its unique features and advantages compared to existing metaheuristic methods.

title: The Mimicry Optimization Algorithm (MOA): Inspired by the Hunting Strategy of Yellow Tang Fish
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimicry Optimization Algorithm (MOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategy of the Yellow Tang fish (*Paracopropodichthys galaxias*). Yellow Tang fish are renowned for their remarkable ability to herd prey into confined spaces, effectively trapping them. MOA leverages this behavior through a multi-faceted approach involving adaptive agent positioning, dynamic obstacle manipulation, and a mimicking mechanism. The algorithm employs a population of 'mimic' agents, each tasked with mimicking the movement patterns of 'leader' agents, which themselves are strategically positioned based on the landscape of the optimization problem. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates a 'pressure' mechanism to dynamically adjust the difficulty of the environment, simulating the prey's attempts to escape. The core of MOA lies in its 'Mimicry Score' function, which quantifies the effectiveness of an agent's mimicry and guides the agent's movement towards optimal solutions. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and the underlying principles governing its operation, offering a potential alternative for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Probabilistic Programming with Causal Bayesian Networks for Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Counterfactual reasoning – the ability to reason about "what if" scenarios – is a cornerstone of human intelligence and a critical component in many fields, including medicine, economics, and artificial intelligence. Traditional probabilistic programming approaches often struggle to effectively address counterfactual queries, largely due to the inherent difficulties in explicitly modeling causal relationships. This paper introduces a novel framework combining probabilistic programming with causal Bayesian networks to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to allow users to directly specify causal dependencies between variables within a probabilistic programming environment, enabling efficient simulation and the generation of realistic counterfactual scenarios. The proposed system provides a powerful tool for understanding the causal impact of different events, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques. We demonstrate the framework's capabilities through illustrative examples, highlighting its potential for a wide range of applications. The system leverages techniques from Bayesian networks to represent causal relationships and probabilistic programming to perform simulations and queries. This allows for the derivation of counterfactual probabilities and the exploration of alternative scenarios. The overall goal is to facilitate more robust and interpretable reasoning about complex systems.

abstract: This paper introduces the Northeast Forest Frog-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (NFF-MHOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to mimic the foraging behavior and adaptability of the Northeast Forest Frog (*Lithobates japonicus*) in a complex and dynamic environment. The algorithm leverages key aspects of the frog's hunting strategy, including opportunistic movement, territory defense, and response to environmental changes, to generate a robust and efficient search process. NFF-MHOA incorporates three primary mechanisms: a territory-based population representation, an adaptive movement strategy based on environmental assessment, and a dynamic response mechanism for tackling local optima. While lacking experimental validation, this paper provides a theoretical framework and detailed algorithm description, highlighting the core principles and potential advantages of NFF-MHOA for solving various optimization problems. The algorithm's design aims to improve convergence speed, robustness, and adaptability compared to traditional metaheuristic approaches.

title: ## The Yellow-Crowned Crane Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (YCMHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Yellow-Crowned Crane Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (YCMHOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and social dynamics of the Yellow-Crowned Crane. The algorithm leverages the crane's cyclical movement patterns, its tendency to explore and exploit, and its collaborative decision-making processes to achieve efficient and robust optimization. YCMHOA employs a population-based approach with a unique 'Circle-and-Spiral' movement strategy, combining exploration and exploitation phases. The algorithm incorporates a 'Social Influence Factor' to model the cooperative behavior and a 'Spiral Density' parameter to control the exploration rate. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual overview of its operation. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the spiral's parameters based on the population's convergence rate, mimicking the crane's adaptive responses to environmental changes and resource availability. The algorithm's potential applications across various optimization problems are discussed.

title: African Long-fingered Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bat-Inspired Adaptive Optimization Algorithm" (BIAOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the African long-fingered bat ( *Longipedotus swalesi*). The core mechanics of the algorithm are based on the bats' frequency and phase adjustments, mimicking their search for food. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a population of potential solutions, represented as vectors, and employs a dynamic adjustment of frequency and phase parameters to guide the search process. The frequency represents the exploration ability, and the phase represents the exploitation ability. The algorithm incorporates adaptive parameters to control the balance between exploration and exploitation, enhancing its robustness and convergence speed. The performance of BIAOA is evaluated through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for practical applications. The key contributions of this work include the detailed formulation of the algorithm, its theoretical analysis, and its empirical validation, showcasing its superior performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The algorithm's adaptive nature and bat-inspired mechanics offer a promising approach to tackling challenging optimization tasks.

title: Addax-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed Addax-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AIMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Addax antelope. The Addax, a resilient desert animal, exhibits remarkable efficiency in locating scarce resources under challenging environmental conditions. This paper leverages these adaptive strategies, specifically the Addax's ability to assess resource quality and prioritize exploration, to design a new optimization algorithm. AIMA incorporates three key mechanisms: Resource Quality Assessment (RQA), Adaptive Exploration-Exploitation (AEE), and a dynamic memory component mimicking the Addax's learned knowledge of favorable resource locations. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. Results demonstrate that AIMA consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in high-dimensional and complex landscapes. The core of the algorithm revolves around the concept of 'resource quality' – a measure of the fitness value at a given solution point. The AEE mechanism dynamically adjusts the balance between exploration and exploitation based on this quality assessment, ensuring efficient convergence while avoiding premature convergence to local optima. The dynamic memory component stores the locations of high-quality resources, guiding the search towards promising areas of the solution space. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through detailed analysis of convergence rates, solution accuracy, and computational efficiency. The presented algorithm offers a potentially valuable tool for tackling complex optimization challenges in various domains.

title: Core Claim: A Quantum Entanglement-Based Adaptive Topological Transformation
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a paradigm shift in computation, potentially enabling fundamentally more efficient algorithms and models. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to adaptive topological transformation, a novel approach designed to enhance computational performance. We detail a method utilizing entangled states to dynamically reshape topological structures, offering a pathway towards improved efficiency and accuracy in various computational tasks. The core mechanism centers around leveraging entanglement to iteratively modify the topological properties of a system, achieving transformations without explicit, computationally intensive calculations. This research investigates the potential benefits of this approach, focusing on its theoretical foundations and experimental implications. We present a preliminary design and analysis demonstrating the feasibility of this technique, highlighting its potential for future advancements in quantum computing and data processing.

title: Predictive Coding with Temporal Convolutional Networks
abstract: Predictive coding frameworks, while conceptually appealing for modeling cognitive processes, often face challenges in accurately representing temporal dependencies within sequential data. This work addresses this limitation by proposing a novel approach that integrates predictive coding principles with the strengths of Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs). The core idea centers around a TCN that learns to predict future input sequences based on past observations, leveraging dilated convolutions to effectively capture long-range temporal correlations. This combined architecture demonstrates improved predictive accuracy compared to traditional predictive coding models. The methodology details a specific TCN architecture optimized for temporal prediction, and presents preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this approach. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of these two techniques, offering a potentially more robust and accurate method for modeling temporal sequences.

title: Adaptive Quantum State-Based Partial Differential Equations
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to solving partial differential equations (PDEs) utilizing adaptive quantum state manipulation. Traditional methods often struggle with complex quantum state configurations, limiting their applicability to problems involving intricate spacetime geometries. This research proposes a method that leverages the unique properties of quantum states to optimize the numerical solution process, resulting in improved accuracy and the ability to handle PDEs with dynamically evolving quantum states. The core mechanism centers around a quantum state transformation process that iteratively adjusts the state to better represent the PDE's solution, enhancing the numerical stability and precision. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of numerical simulations focusing on a simplified, yet representative, PDE problem. The results showcase a significant improvement in accuracy compared to existing numerical methods, particularly in scenarios involving high-dimensional quantum states.

title: Learning Among Learners: A Narrative Review of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Markov Games to Deep Emergent Play
abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning---the learning of behavior when the environment's other agents learn too---moved from Tan's independent learners and Littman's Markov games framework through the cooperative dynamics' analyses and the surveys' question to the deep era's communication, actor-critics, value decompositions, and the large-scale emergent play of Capture the Flag. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Tan's 1993 independent versus cooperative agents, Littman's 1994 Markov games, Claus and Boutilier's 1998 cooperative dynamics, Hu and Wellman's 1998 framework, Shoham, Powers, and Grenager's 2007 question, Busoniu, Babuska, and De Schutter's 2008 survey, Foerster and colleagues' 2016 learning to communicate, Lowe and colleagues' 2017 multi-agent actor-critic, Sunehag and colleagues' 2018 value-decomposition networks, Rashid and colleagues' 2018 QMIX, Jaderberg and colleagues' 2019 3D multiplayer Capture the Flag, and Hernandez-Leal, Kartal, and Taylor's 2019 survey and critique. The review is organized around three themes: the foundational frames, in which the Markov game's formalization and the non-stationarity's, the coordination's, and the equilibrium's problems defined the field's difficulties; the theory's question, in which the surveys asked what learning among learners is for; and the deep era, in which the communications, the centralized critics, the monotonic factorizations, and the population-scale play made the multi-agent learning practical. It is concluded that multi-agent reinforcement learning is the non-stationarity's discipline---and that its deep era turned the other learners' obstruction into the curriculum's engine.

title: XAI2CSI: Interpreting CSI with eXplainable AI for Human Activity Recognition
abstract: Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) has emerged as a key enabler for device-free Human Activity Recognition (HAR), enabling low-cost, unobtrusive sensing using existing communication infrastructure. However, Deep Learning (DL) models trained on CSI data often struggle to generalize across users, environments, and device setups due to the context sensitivity of wireless propagation. Despite this challenge, limited attention has been devoted to understanding model decisions and generalization failures. This paper introduces XAI2CSI, a framework that leverages eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to analyze DL-based CSI sensing systems. XAI2CSI employs SAGE, a model-agnostic explainability method, to quantify temporal, spectral, and spatial CSI contributions to HAR decisions under nominal and cross-context evaluations on IEEE 802.11ax data. Our analysis reveals that the considered DL model exhibits limited robustness to unseen conditions due to an over-reliance on context-specific CSI patterns, causing models to misinterpret the underlying signal dynamics when deployment conditions change. The proposed methodology and findings provide a reference framework to explore alternative solutions and guide the development of robust, transparent Wi-Fi sensing systems.

title: Audio-Driven Adversarial Defense for 3D Talking Face Generation with totally Visual Fidelity Preservation
abstract: The rapid development of generative portrait models has raised growing concerns about privacy leakage and identity misuse. In particular, audio-driven 3D talking face generation can reconstruct a reusable 3D portrait of a target person from a monocular video and animate it with arbitrary speech, making realistic identity impersonation alarmingly practical. Existing proactive defenses mainly operate in the visual domain by injecting subtle perturbations into acial regions to disrupt identity acquisition. However, such perturbations often compromise visual quality due to the strong structural priors and social sensitivity of human faces, and are easily weakened by common real-world transformations such as resizing. To overcome these limitations, we propose an imperceptible audio defense for audio-driven 3D talking face generation by shifting protection from the visual modality to the audio modality. Specifically,we exploit psychoacoustic masking to hide protective perturbations within perceptually masked frequency regions of the speech signal, thereby reducing perceptual distortion while suppressing reliable facial animation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method effectively degrades 3D talking face generation while preserving favorable perceptual quality. These findings highlight psychoacoustically guided audio perturbations as a practical and promising direction for privacy-preserving portrait protection.

title: WildSEEK: Evaluating Language Models for Information-Seeking
abstract: Language models are increasingly mediating information access to end users, urging a systematic evaluation of their responses for a fair and reliable information ecosystem. Existing evaluations, however, are often topic-specific or synthetic, limiting their ability to capture the complexity of "in the wild" information-seeking queries and the risks present in model responses. To address this gap, we introduce WildSEEK, a manually annotated dataset of 3k information-seeking queries from real user interactions, and an evaluation framework for LLM-generated responses. WildSEEK includes annotations for risk-sensitive domains (e.g. health and financial information), and distinguishes factoid queries from analytical queries which seek responses beyond facts. We train classifiers on WildSEEK to analyze more than 1.8M realistic user queries. We find that over a third of information-seeking queries are high-risk and more often analytical. Our findings show that LLM responses fail more often in four criteria: sycophantic behavior, overreliance, a default US-centric perspective, and poor handling of vulnerable populations -- with failure rates being mostly higher for analytical queries. By providing methods to monitor the reliability, safety, and fairness of LLM behavior, our dataset and evaluation framework offer an empirical foundation for the broader question of how these systems should behave as they take on a growing role in information access.

title: BiG-SURE - Bipartite Graph for Semantic Uncertainty and Reliability Estimation of LLMs
abstract: Reliable uncertainty estimation is a crucial requirement for deploying large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) in safety-critical settings, especially when the model parameters are not accessible (black-box). We propose BiG-SURE, an uncertainty estimator based on cross-temperature semantic agreement. The method samples low-temperature responses as stable semantic anchors and high-temperature responses as probes under meaning-preserving input transformations. It then constructs an anchor-probe Bipartite Graph (BiG) using NLI-based entailment scores and defines confidence through the normalized squared spectral energy of this matrix, with uncertainty given by its complement. This bipartite graph-based Semantic Uncertainty and Reliability Estimation (SURE) score measures whether high-temperature probes remain semantically aligned with the model's stable low-temperature belief or not. We evaluate BiG-SURE on text QA, multilingual QA, and multimodal QA tasks across multiple model families. In these experiments, BiG-SURE improves average abstention AUROC over prior black-box uncertainty estimators, while remaining simple, unsupervised, and applicable to black-box model settings.

title: Efficient measurement schemes for the Monte Carlo projective quantum eigensolver
abstract: The Monte Carlo Projective Quantum Eigensolver (MC-PQE) was recently introduced as an alternative to hybrid algorithms like the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). By using a quantum Monte Carlo-inspired scheme for energy estimation, MC\nobreakdash-PQE was found to decrease the required measurement cost relative to comparable conventional approaches. However, in the context of VQE, numerous techniques have been developed to reduce the measurement overhead by joint measurement of multiple observables. In this work, we extend these approaches to the asymmetric expectation values required in MC-PQE and assess the performance of different techniques for various molecular systems of up to 12 qubits. We find full commuting Pauli term grouping combined with tailored measurement allocation techniques leads to a 5-10$\times$ reduction in standard error for the same total number of quantum measurements. Conventional Hamiltonian grouped measurement outperforms tractable classical shadows tomography based techniques for the considered systems.

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Use on Reservation Systems in the Tourism Sector in Egypt (An Applied Study on Customers of Tourism Offices in Cairo)
abstract: هدفت الدراسة إلى التعرف على أثر استخدام تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي على نظم الحجز في قطاع السياحة من وجهة نظر العملاء، مع دراسة تأثير متغيرات العمر والمستوى الدراسي والدخل. اعتمدت الدراسة على المنهجين الوصفي والتحليلي، حيث تم توزيع استبانة إلكترونية على عملاء مكاتب السياحة في مدينة القاهرة، وتم استرجاع 337 استبانة بنسبة 87.8%، وتم تحليل البيانات باستخدام برنامج SPSS من خلال الإحصاءات الوصفية والانحدار الخطي المتعدد واختبارات الارتباط والتعددية (VIF وTolerance). أظهرت النتائج ارتفاع مستوى اهتمام العملاء بالذكاء الاصطناعي ونظم الحجز، كما بينت أن جميع أبعاد الذكاء الاصطناعي، بما في ذلك النظم الخبيرة، الخوارزميات الجينية، تمثيل المعرفة والاستدلال، التعلم العميق، والروبوتات، لها أثر ذو دلالة إحصائية على نظم الحجز في قطاع السياحة. وبناءً على النتائج، أوصت الدراسة بتطوير نظم خبيرة لتقديم استشارات دقيقة وفورية للعملاء، ودمج تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي في البنية التحتية للحجز لتحسين رحلة العميل وجودة الخدمة، بالإضافة إلى استخدام الخوارزميات الجينية لإنشاء برامج رحلات مخصصة ومتوازنة بين التكلفة والوقت وشركات الطيران

title: Treinamento de Inteligências Artificiais Generativas com ativos distintivos da propriedade industrial: limites jurídicos e lacunas regulatórias no Brasil
abstract: O avanço da Inteligência Artificial Generativa (IAG) intensificou o debate sobre o uso de ativos protegidos durante o treinamento de grandes modelos de linguagem, concentrando-se, contudo, nos direitos autorais. Este estudo analisa a lacuna regulatória relativa à utilização de ativos distintivos da propriedade industrial, especialmente marcas, marcas de certificação e indicações geográficas, no treinamento desses sistemas. Adotou-se abordagem qualitativa, exploratória e descritiva, fundamentada em pesquisa bibliográfica, documental e em Direito Comparado, com análise da legislação brasileira, do Projeto de Lei nº 2.338/2023 e dos modelos regulatórios dos Estados Unidos, União Europeia e China. Os resultados evidenciam que o ordenamento jurídico brasileiro protege esses ativos em sua exploração econômica tradicional, mas permanece insuficiente para disciplinar sua utilização como insumos informacionais na economia baseada em dados. Conclui-se pela necessidade de um marco regulatório que incorpore transparência, rastreabilidade, governança dos dados e proteção dos ativos distintivos, conciliando inovação tecnológica, segurança jurídica e desenvolvimento econômico.

title: कतरम बदधमतत (AI) आण मनव मनसशसतर : मनसशसतरय परणम, सध व आवहनच समकषतमक आढव
abstract: कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (Artificial Intelligence-AI) ही आधुनिक तंत्रज्ञानातील वेगाने विकसित होणारी प्रणाली असून तिचा मानवी जीवनाच्या विविध क्षेत्रांबरोबरच मानसशास्त्रीय प्रक्रियांवरही वाढता प्रभाव दिसून येत आहे. प्रस्तुत पुनरावलोकनात्मक अभ्यासाचा उद्देश AI आणि मानवी मानसशास्त्र यांच्यातील परस्परसंबंधाचा आढावा घेणे तसेच AI मुळे निर्माण होणारे संज्ञानात्मक, भावनिक, वर्तनात्मक आणि सामाजिक परिणाम, मानसिक आरोग्यावरील प्रभाव, संधी आणि आव्हाने यांचे विश्लेषण करणे हा आहे. अभ्यासासाठी संरचित साहित्य पुनरावलोकन (Structured Literature Review) पद्धतीचा अवलंब करण्यात आला असून Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, ScienceDirect आणि Google Scholar या डेटाबेसमधील संबंधित संशोधन साहित्याचा विचार करण्यात आला. साहित्य निवड प्रक्रियेत PRISMA 2020 मार्गदर्शक तत्त्वांचा आधार घेण्यात आला. उपलब्ध संशोधनाच्या आढाव्यातून AI मुळे संज्ञानात्मक सहाय्य, वैयक्तिकृत शिक्षण, मानसिक आरोग्य सेवा आणि कार्यक्षमता वाढविण्याच्या संधी उपलब्ध होत असल्याचे दिसून आले. त्याचवेळी AI वरील अवलंबित्व, संज्ञानात्मक भार-हस्तांतरण, AI विषयीची चिंता, सामाजिक अलगाव, गोपनीयता, मानवी स्वायत्तता, पक्षपात आणि रोजगार असुरक्षितता यांसारखी आव्हानेही अधोरेखित झाली. भारतीय संदर्भात भाषिक, सांस्कृतिक आणि डिजिटल विषमता विचारात घेणे आवश्यक आहे. त्यामुळे AI चा मानवकेंद्री, संतुलित आणि नैतिक वापर मानवी मानसिक कल्याणासाठी अत्यावश्यक असल्याचे पुनरावलोकनातून निष्पन्न होते.

title: Recommended Network of Semantic Resources for the Food Supply Chains
abstract: IntroductionThis document provides guidance for stakeholders in the food supply chain to identify and access relevant semantic resources when integrating a semantic layer into their digital solutions.The recommended semantic resources—forming a network of shared resources for the agricultural and food supply chains—has the potential to create a standardized and interoperable framework that integrates and harmonizes data across stakeholders. PurposeAdopting shared semantic resources enables data integration and interoperability among food supply chain actors—and, ultimately, across all supply chains. This approach ensures that all stakeholders interpret data and its relationships consistently, supporting seamless communication, collaboration, and more efficient decision-making.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic quantum state optimization algorithm designed to efficiently optimize quantum states and enhance precise control. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter settings, limiting their applicability to complex systems. This work proposes a dynamic approach that leverages quantum state's inherent adaptability to dynamically adjust quantum states, leading to improved optimization performance. The core mechanism involves a combination of quantum state self-adaptation and a tailored topology optimization algorithm, demonstrating significant improvements in achieving precise control and optimization accuracy. This algorithm addresses limitations of existing approaches, offering a more robust and adaptable solution for quantum state manipulation.

title: Dynamic Probability Field Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic probability field model designed to simulate complex system behavior and predict future states by dynamically adjusting probability field parameters based on real-time data and environmental changes. Leveraging the integration of machine learning and reinforcement learning, this model offers a significant advancement over traditional probabilistic models, enabling automated parameter tuning and real-time system modeling. The core mechanism focuses on continuously adapting probability field configurations, leading to enhanced prediction accuracy and efficiency. This work addresses a critical need for systems capable of robust and adaptable behavior in dynamic environments.

title: Dynamic Quantum State-Based Topological Coding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to topological coding based on dynamic quantum state evolution. We develop a system that encodes quantum information using the inherent properties of quantum states, enabling efficient quantum information transmission and manipulation through quantum entanglement. The core mechanism involves dynamically altering the quantum state to represent information, leveraging topological properties to enhance quantum computations. This research explores the potential of integrating dynamic quantum states with topological structures to significantly improve the speed and efficiency of quantum information processing. The resulting system demonstrates enhanced encoding capabilities and offers a promising path toward advancing quantum technologies.

title: Adaptive Quantum Self-Adaptation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for exponential speedups over classical computing, but current algorithms often struggle to reach this potential due to the complexities of managing quantum states and the inherent limitations of quantum hardware. This paper introduces the Adaptive Quantum Self-Adaptation Algorithm (ASFAA), a novel quantum control strategy designed to dynamically adjust quantum operations based on the system's state. The algorithm leverages a self-adaptive mechanism to continuously refine quantum parameters, optimizing for improved performance and robustness. We present a theoretical framework for the algorithm's operation, demonstrating its ability to achieve significant efficiency gains in various quantum systems through automated parameter adjustments. The core claim of this research is that ASFAA provides a pathway to efficient quantum computation by automating the optimization of quantum gate parameters. This advancement addresses a critical challenge in quantum algorithm design and opens possibilities for more practical and scalable quantum computations.

title: Distributed Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance via Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed machine learning that achieves Byzantine fault tolerance by leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). The core challenge in distributed learning environments is the vulnerability to malicious nodes introducing erroneous updates, leading to compromised model accuracy. Our proposed system constructs a graph representing the network of learning nodes and utilizes GNNs for communication and aggregation. Specifically, the GNNs filter out malicious updates by learning node embeddings that capture the trustworthiness of each node's contribution. This allows the system to learn a robust global model even when a significant proportion of nodes are acting maliciously. We formulate the problem as a robust aggregation process guided by the GNN's learned node representations. The system's performance is evaluated theoretically and analytically, demonstrating its resilience to Byzantine attacks and its ability to converge towards a correct global model. The key contribution lies in the integration of Byzantine fault tolerance with the expressive power of GNNs, offering a scalable and reliable solution for decentralized learning applications.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Topological Adaptation for Dynamic System Modeling
abstract: Quantum-enhanced topological adaptation represents a paradigm shift in system modeling, moving beyond static representations to dynamically shape the model's geometric structure, thereby mirroring the complexities of evolving systems. This paper explores the concept of a "Quantum Topology Engine" – a novel algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to subtly adjust the system's topology, offering a pathway to more accurate and responsive dynamic system simulations. We present a theoretical framework outlining the core mechanics, discuss the potential benefits and challenges, and outline a preliminary experimental validation strategy. The research focuses on establishing a foundation for future investigations into the application of quantum-assisted topological modeling to dynamic system analysis.

title: Causal Inference from Multi-Modal Data Streams
abstract: This paper explores the application of causal inference techniques to multi-modal data streams, aiming to establish more accurate causal models for prediction and control in complex systems. Traditional single-modality causal inference methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and ambiguity present in real-world scenarios where information is conveyed through diverse sources like vision, audio, and text. This research proposes a framework that leverages the temporal dependencies within multi-modal data streams to identify causal relationships. The core of the approach involves employing causal discovery algorithms to automatically uncover these relationships within the data, followed by structured probabilistic modeling for reasoning and time-series analysis for prediction. The novelty lies in the integration of multiple modalities, allowing for a more nuanced and robust understanding of causal dynamics compared to traditional methods. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and methodological considerations. Further research will focus on developing specific algorithms and evaluating the framework's performance on real-world datasets.

title: 基于量子态的模式识别算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel pattern recognition algorithm based on quantum state manipulation, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve rapid identification and modeling of complex patterns, particularly in large and high-dimensional datasets. Traditional pattern recognition methods rely on classical information retrieval, which suffers from inefficiency. We propose a quantum-enhanced approach that utilizes quantum state manipulation to drastically improve data analysis efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism centers around the utilization of quantum entanglement to facilitate efficient pattern recognition and representation. This paper details the design of the algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential for significant improvements in pattern analysis.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Non-Linear Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement principles. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, non-linear problems, demanding extensive manual tuning. This algorithm leverages quantum entanglement to establish a dynamic interaction between parameters, enabling a more adaptive and robust solution strategy. We propose a mechanism that iteratively adjusts parameters based on entanglement correlations, facilitating the exploration of complex solution spaces and improving the performance of various optimization tasks, particularly those encountered in machine learning, financial modeling, and risk management. The core of this approach lies in the manipulation of entanglement to achieve a more efficient and nuanced optimization process. This research explores the potential of quantum entanglement to surpass the limitations of classical optimization techniques.

title: 基于非线性自适应的机器学习模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning model based on non-linear adaptive learning. The model incorporates a self-adaptive optimization algorithm to dynamically adjust model parameters, enabling efficient optimization even with large and noisy datasets. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness through a series of experiments evaluating its performance on diverse datasets, showcasing its ability to automatically tune parameters and achieve superior results compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism involves a non-linear adaptive algorithm that iteratively adjusts model parameters based on observed error, while the self-adaptive optimization algorithm ensures optimal parameter values. We provide a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance and highlight its advantages in scenarios demanding rapid adaptation and robust performance.

title: Quantum Error Mitigation Techniques for Complex Algorithms
abstract: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) is a crucial step in developing quantum algorithms, aiming to reduce the impact of errors during computation. However, complex algorithms often exhibit significant errors, necessitating sophisticated mitigation strategies. This paper explores the application of novel QEM techniques, focusing on a dynamically adjustable system to minimize errors within complex algorithms. We propose a design that adapts to the specific error characteristics of the algorithm, enhancing accuracy and providing a more robust solution compared to existing approaches. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors and adjusts the algorithm's parameters to counteract errors, resulting in improved performance. This work presents a conceptual framework for a transformative QEM approach, demonstrating the potential for significant accuracy gains through intelligent adaptation.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Simulation-Based Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Simulation-based reinforcement learning (SBRL) has emerged as a powerful technique for training agents in complex environments where real-world interaction is costly or dangerous. However, the performance of SBRL is heavily reliant on the accuracy and fidelity of the underlying simulation environment. This work proposes a novel approach to SBRL that leverages probabilistic programming languages (PPLs) to explicitly model and reason about uncertainty within the simulation. By representing the simulation environment as a probabilistic model, agents can not only learn optimal policies but also quantify and adapt to the inherent uncertainties present in the simulated world. This allows for a more robust and adaptive SBRL system, addressing a critical limitation of traditional methods. The core claim is that incorporating uncertainty modeling through PPLs dramatically improves the performance and adaptability of SBRL. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework and outline key considerations for implementation. ---

title: 基于图的量子机器学习的拓扑结构建模
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum machine learning framework based on topological structure modeling. Traditional machine learning methods often rely on human-designed algorithms, limiting their adaptability and efficiency. We propose a new approach that leverages graph theory and topology to automatically discover and optimize quantum machine learning algorithms. This framework allows us to effectively model complex system topological structures and predict their behavior. The core mechanism focuses on identifying and exploiting the inherent structural properties of quantum systems through graph-based representations, fostering enhanced computational performance and predictive capabilities. This work represents a significant advancement in the field of quantum machine learning, offering a robust and automated methodology for topological analysis and quantum algorithm design.

title: Bengal Loris-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BLIMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Bengal Loris-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BLIMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Bengal Lorises ( *Nyctales bengalensis*). Bengal Lorises are known for their unique and efficient foraging strategies, utilizing a combination of visual and olfactory cues to locate food sources with remarkable speed and accuracy. BLIMA leverages these key aspects of lorises' behavior – specifically, their 'scanning' search pattern, their adaptive response to environmental changes, and their ability to prioritize promising areas – to construct a new optimization algorithm. The algorithm incorporates a 'scanning' mechanism mimicking the lorises' visual sweeps, an adaptive parameter adjustment system reflecting their responsiveness to changes in scent concentration, and a prioritization scheme based on a 'likelihood score' similar to their preference for areas with higher food density. We demonstrate the efficacy of BLIMA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP), the Rastrigin Function, and the Sphere Function. The results show that BLIMA achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in problems exhibiting complex landscapes and dynamic changes. The core of BLIMA lies in its ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on the perceived "density" of potential solutions, an adaptation inspired by the lorises' foraging prowess. The algorithm's performance is analyzed, and its potential applications are discussed.

title: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Beech Marten Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Beech Marten Foraging Algorithm" (BMFA), inspired by the foraging behavior of beech martens. Beech martens are known for their intelligent and adaptive search strategies when locating food sources. BMFA utilizes a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms. The algorithm incorporates a novel 'trail marking' mechanism mimicking a beech marten's ability to remember and revisit promising areas. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the exploration and exploitation phases based on the 'trail strength' associated with each potential solution. This trail strength is proportional to the solution's fitness and the number of iterations it has been explored. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. Experimental results indicate that BMFA consistently outperforms traditional PSO and ABC algorithms in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's parameters are tuned using a grey wolf optimization method for enhanced performance. title: Quantum Computing Through Time Constant Optimization
abstract: Quantum computing promises a revolutionary leap in computational power, but its practical realization hinges critically on the control and manipulation of quantum bits (qubits). A significant bottleneck in achieving this potential is the inherent variability in qubit coherence times – often referred to as time constants. These time constants, denoted as *τ*, represent the duration for which a qubit maintains its quantum state before decoherence sets in, directly impacting the fidelity of quantum computations. This work explores the concept of optimizing these time constants to enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. We delve into the mechanisms that govern *τ* within various qubit systems and propose a novel algorithmic approach to dynamically adjust qubit parameters, aiming to minimize *τ* and maximize the duration of quantum operations. The core contribution lies in recognizing *τ* as a primary performance determinant and outlining a systematic strategy for its targeted improvement. The presented framework offers a potential pathway toward realizing the full potential of quantum computing by mitigating the detrimental effects of decoherence.

title: Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Optimization and Genetic Programming
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to symbolic regression, aiming to improve both the accuracy and efficiency of equation discovery. The core idea is to integrate Bayesian optimization with genetic programming, creating a hybrid system. Bayesian optimization is used to guide the search for potentially good equation forms, effectively narrowing down the vast solution space. Genetic programming then utilizes this guided information to evolve and refine those forms, leveraging the strengths of both techniques. We propose a framework where Bayesian optimization iteratively suggests promising equation structures, and genetic programming evolves them, resulting in a more targeted and robust search process. This combined approach addresses limitations inherent in traditional symbolic regression methods and demonstrates the potential to uncover complex mathematical relationships that might otherwise be missed. The experimental results, while not presented through formal experimentation, strongly suggest the viability and efficacy of this combined methodology.

title: ##基于多智能体强化学习的机器人群组控制
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to the control of robot swarms for complex task execution. Traditional robot swarm control methods often rely on manually designed control strategies, which can be difficult to adapt to dynamic and uncertain environments. This research proposes a novel approach where a robot swarm is treated as a collection of individual agents, each learning its own action policy through MARL. The core mechanism involves decentralized learning, enabling the swarm to achieve coordinated behavior and perform complex tasks without explicit, centralized control. This work presents a framework for MARL-based robot swarm control, demonstrating its potential for robustness and adaptability in challenging scenarios. The primary focus is on the theoretical foundations and conceptual design, without experimental validation, aiming to provide a robust and scalable methodology for future research and development.

title: Aru Flying Fox: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Flight of the Flying Fox
abstract: This paper presents Aru Flying Fox (AFF), a new metaheuristic algorithm designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the remarkable flight capabilities of the flying fox (Pteropus), a large fruit bat known for its precise maneuvering and efficient energy expenditure during flight. title: ## The Ripple Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Inspired by the Behavior of Pufferfish
abstract: This paper introduces the Ripple Algorithm, a novel metaheuristic optimization method inspired by the foraging behavior of pufferfish ( *Tetraodontidae* ). Pufferfish are known for their remarkable ability to locate and efficiently exploit food sources in complex environments, utilizing a strategy involving rhythmic "ripples" – localized disturbances in the water – to detect prey. The Ripple Algorithm mimics this process by iteratively generating and evaluating candidate solutions, modifying them based on a "ripple" mechanism that propagates changes throughout the search space. The algorithm's core components include a 'ripple amplitude' parameter controlling the extent of solution modification, a 'ripple frequency' dictating the rate of propagation, and a 'ripple decay' factor influencing the dissipation of the ripple effect. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, explains its operational principles, and outlines its potential applications in various optimization problems. We aim to demonstrate that this bio-inspired approach offers a robust and adaptable method for tackling challenging optimization landscapes.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Dynamic Topological Networks
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to information encoding leveraging quantum entanglement within a dynamically controlled topological network. The core concept involves harnessing the non-local nature of entanglement to achieve transmission rates exceeding those attainable through classical channels. We propose a system where entangled nodes are strategically positioned within a network exhibiting non-exchangeable connections. Dynamic adjustments to the network topology—specifically, modifying the connections between nodes—are employed to manipulate the entangled states, thereby facilitating information encoding and decoding. The key innovation lies in the integration of entanglement information encoding with topological network dynamic control, addressing the limitations of static topological networks and the fragility of entangled states. Mathematical models are presented to describe the system's behavior, focusing on the manipulation of entanglement and the impact of network topology on information transfer. We demonstrate the potential for significantly enhanced information throughput by exploiting the inherent properties of quantum entanglement and the adaptability of topological networks. The proposed framework offers a pathway to robust and high-speed quantum communication.

title: Quantum Information Theory: Adaptive Learning of Topological Geometry
abstract: Quantum information theory has witnessed significant advancements in recent years, primarily focusing on the development of quantum algorithms and their applications. However, a deeper investigation into the underlying principles governing these systems often overlooks a crucial and potentially transformative aspect: the role of topological geometry. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum information theory to enable adaptive learning and optimization within the context of topological geometry, driven by quantum entanglement and the inherent properties of topological structures. This work investigates a novel mechanism for quantum state learning and optimization, leveraging the power of quantum entanglement and topological geometry to achieve rapid adaptation and improved performance.

title: 基于自适应的自组织神经网络结构优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for optimizing the structure of self-organizing neural networks (SONNs) through dynamic adjustment of connection strengths. Traditional SONNs often rely on manually defined layer configurations, which can be suboptimal and require significant tuning. Our proposed algorithm, termed "Adaptive Resonance Network Optimization" (ARNO), employs a self-adaptive reinforcement learning approach to automatically adjust connection weights, leading to improved network performance across various tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ARNO through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing significant gains in accuracy and efficiency compared to baseline methods. The core mechanism involves iteratively adjusting connection strengths based on a learned reward function, enabling the network to converge to an optimal configuration.
